Despite the mutual hatred, they are forced to negotiate: Fex require the spans to transport coal and machinery across the chasms, while the Groven require Fex cold-iron anchors and geothermal brackets to keep their calcifying bridges from collapsing under the blizzards.

fexrick.diasporaVariation: The Fex are the most widely diasporic non-human race because they built, and maintain, the geothermal infrastructure connecting every region. Brasskin guild-halls exist in every capital (Merrowport, Greymark, Atropolis, the Frozen Archive, Harath-Vault, Synod Hold), each staffed by Brasskin who have lived local for generations and speak the local tongue with a Fex accent. These diaspora Brasskin are culturally flexible in a way the Frostmaw-pure Brasskin distrust. The Alchemite clan-nomads roam between all regions on maintenance-circuits and are functionally a trans-national people, an Alchemite speaks seven regional dialects and claims no capital.
fexrick.meaningfulTradeoffs: Fex craft and oral knowledge pair with conductive-graft vulnerability and the recorded Still-Air limitations. Guild secrecy, Groven relations and Sumpborn recognition offer political conflicts without making every engineer responsible for every experiment.

baseTraits.build: Compact and stocky, pale green or mine-darkened skin, elaborate beards woven with tools and copper wire, one visible mechanical replacement

createdPeoples.name: Sumpborn
createdPeoples.origin: Sapient people emerging from heavy-metal alchemical runoff, distinct from native Fex

fexrick.epicHistory:
In the Long Before, native Fex settled Cragjaw after the Thrumm and built holdfast machinery around Vurath's power. Their maintained infrastructure is ancient; it does not prove they predate all native peoples or invented the primordial engine. Maintenance songs preserve crafted techniques and incomplete knowledge of a source older than the machines.

Old holdfast networks expanded through native Thrumm territory. Fex machinery provided ventilation, pumping and structural support around an older source of power. Territorial conflict and later experiments do not reverse the order of settlement: Thrumm preceded the Fex, and Groven emerged from captured broodlings rather than primordial Fex invention of all stone life.

The surface was never a priority. The Fex knew it existed, maintenance shafts occasionally breached open air, but the surface was cold, bright, and irrelevant. When humans arrived and built their keeps in the Cragjaw, the Fex watched from below and did not interfere. When the sun died and the freeze began, the Fex barely noticed. They had never depended on the sun.

When the noble family struck the dark bargain, trading visibility for the eternal snow-veil, the Fex's few surface outposts were sealed by the blizzard. The Fex sealed the connecting tunnels and continued their work. The surface was the surface's problem.

The Deep Alchemists emerged as a distinct guild roughly two thousand years ago, when the first signs of machine-decay were documented. The oldest turbines, the ones from the first holdfast, the ones whose original builders had been dead for five millennia, were beginning to slow. The maintenance songs for those turbines were incomplete, the oral tradition having degraded across thousands of years of transmission. The Alchemists proposed radical solutions: reverse-engineering the machines, experimenting with new compounds, testing whether new machine-life could be cultivated from old. The Orthodoxy, the alliance of traditional guilds, condemned this as heresy. The schism has never healed.

The Groven were created before the sun was buried. The Alchemists, working in secret laboratories in the lowest sumps, had been capturing Thrumm broodlings for decades, injecting them with serums designed to smooth their stone-hide into fine scales, lengthen their limbs for reaching across chasms, and awaken higher cognition. The goal was a servitor race, workers who could maintain the machines the Fex themselves were struggling to understand. The first Groven shattered their vats, freed their kin, and fled upward. They built their bridge-civilization in the upper crags. They have never forgiven their creators. The Fex have never forgiven themselves, though most would never say so aloud.

Sumpborn emerged from heavy-metal alchemical runoff in that industrial ecology. Older records called them Fexk scrapfolk, a label easily confused with the playable Fex. Some guilds dismissed them as vermin; author truth recognizes a distinct sapient people. Their scattered salvage communities remain nonplayable in the launch roster.

In the campaign present, failing turbines, incomplete songs and renewed vat operations divide institutions. Groven and Sumpborn are sapient neighbors with histories, not universal monsters or a moral defect of every Fex. Some engineers repair strangers' heat-lines; others hoard knowledge or authorize experiments. Vurath's stirring raises questions the oldest maintenance songs cannot answer.

notableFigures.name: Brasskin Gear-Father
notableFigures.title: The First Tinker
notableFigures.backstory: The legendary founder of the first holdfast, whose name is preserved in the oldest maintenance song still sung. Brasskin designed the original geothermal turbine, a machine so perfectly balanced that it ran for six thousand years before requiring its first major repair. The Guild-Bound subrace is named for him. His mechanical replacement was a brass right hand, built to replace the one he lost in the turbine's initial calibration. The hand is still functional, passed down through his bloodline, worn by the current elder of the First Holdfast. It has outlived seventy-three Fex. It remembers all of them.

notableFigures.name: Alchemite Sump-Scavenger
notableFigures.title: The First Clan-Free
notableFigures.backstory: A Fex born into a collapsed holdfast, orphaned at six, who taught herself tinkering from salvaged Guild scrap and alchemy from mineral runoff the Guilds considered waste. She founded the first Clan-Free workshop in the abandoned sump-tunnels beneath the Third Holdfast, proving that formal guild training was not the only path to mastery. The Guilds denounced her as a heretic. Her inventions, a self-regulating ventilation valve and a mineral-testing paste still in use today, outlived the denunciation. The Clan-Free subrace is named for her.

majorLocations.name: The First Holdfast
majorLocations.description: An ancient maintained industrial heartland, also called Frostmaw Holdfast, with eighteen tiers of workshops, dormitories and machine chambers around geothermal power. Its turbine harnesses a native source rather than proving Fex invented Vurath or preceded every local inhabitant. Guild councils preserve incomplete maintenance songs; Gearhaven is a settlement name and Cog-Spire a building, not a second universal capital.

majorLocations.name: The Sump-Markets
majorLocations.description: A network of Clan-Free trading posts in the abandoned lower tunnels, where Fex outside the guild system barter salvage, alchemical compounds, and improvised tools. The Sump-Markets are the only neutral ground where Guild-Bound and Clan-Free interact as equals, the Guilds need materials the Clan-Free scavenge from the deep, and the Clan-Free need guild-made components they cannot replicate. The markets operate on a strict barter system. Currency is considered a surface affectation.

fexrick.currentCrisis: The oldest machines are failing faster than the oral traditions can be recovered. In the last century alone, three primary turbines, each over five thousand years old, have begun making sounds not documented in any maintenance song. The Guilds debate endlessly: send expeditions to recover lost knowledge from sealed holdfasts, or authorize the Deep Alchemists to attempt experimental repairs. The Clan-Free have begun improvising solutions on their own, using salvage and untested alchemy. The Orthodoxy condemns this as dangerous. The Deep Alchemists watch from their sump-laboratories, waiting for the moment when desperation makes their methods acceptable again. In the deepest level of the oldest holdfast, the First Turbine has begun making a sound like someone trying to remember a song they have not heard in eight thousand years. But last month, for the first time, a secondary turbine in the Fourth Holdfast answered it. The machines are not just failing. They are beginning to communicate. And the frequency they are using is not in any maintenance song; it is a language the Fex have never needed to understand because nothing alive has spoken it since before the holdfasts were carved.
fexrick.culturalPractices: Fex children are apprenticed at age five, earlier for Guild-Bound, later for Clan-Free, but always young. The first tool a Fex child receives is a gear-puller; the first song they learn is the Ventilation Hymn, which calibrates airflow through the holdfast and teaches basic Still-Air awareness. Craft mastery is measured by beards: each achievement adds a copper wire, a gear-tooth, or a braided strand, and a Fex's beard is their public resume. The mechanical replacement is earned at the transition to adulthood, when the apprentice demonstrates mastery of their chosen craft, a brass finger for tinkers, a silver filament for alchemists, a gear-joint for trap-crafters. Clan-Free Fex often build their own replacements from salvage. Marriage is a contract between guilds, not individuals, and the negotiation can take years. The dead are interred inside the machines they tended, their body-heat joining the geothermal flow to power the turbines. A Fex funeral is a maintenance procedure with singing.

sharedTraits.name: Mechanical Interference
sharedTraits.description: Mechanical grafts attract and conduct electrical and chaotic energy: +25% vulnerability to storm and wyrd damage. The copper, brass, and fiber-optic threads woven through your body turn what should be a glancing strike into a full-body circuit.

effects.name: Conductive Grafts
effects.description: +25% storm damage. +25% wyrd damage. Mechanical grafts conduct electrical and chaotic energy with lethal efficiency.

sharedTraits.name: Still-Air Sense
sharedTraits.description: Generations in carefully ventilated holdfasts made you hyper-aware of airflow. You feel the faintest draft, can tell if a tunnel dead-ends or opens into a chamber by air-pressure alone, and instinctively know when ventilation has failed. Advantage on Perception and Survival checks made to navigate underground or detect hidden passages, gas leaks, and structural instability. In stagnant or unventilated spaces, you suffer disadvantage on Concentration checks and feel deeply, irrationally uneasy, the air is wrong, and your body knows it before your mind does.

effects.name: Air-Current Navigation
effects.description: Advantage on Perception and Survival checks to navigate underground, detect hidden passages, gas leaks, and structural instability.

statusEffect.description: You read the air like a map

effects.name: Stagnant Air Unease
effects.description: Disadvantage on Concentration checks in unventilated or stagnant spaces. The air is wrong, and your body knows it.

sharedTraits.name: Conductive Frame
sharedTraits.description: Your mechanical replacement, and the copper, brass, and salvaged metal woven through your body and beard, conducts electrical current with lethal efficiency. Lightning does not merely strike you. It courses through your augmented frame, superheating every metal component in contact with your flesh. You are not just vulnerable to lightning. You are a lodestone for it, and when it finds you, everything metal on your body becomes a brand.

effects.name: Lightning Vulnerability
effects.description: Storm damage is doubled. Your mechanical body parts and woven metal conduct electrical current with catastrophic efficiency.

effects.name: Lodestone Frame
effects.description: When targeted by a lightning-based attack or effect, you are pulled 5 feet toward the source, your augmented frame is drawn to the current. Disadvantage on saving throws to avoid lightning effects.

kethrin.name: Brasskin
kethrin.illustrationCaption: “The escapement heart does not hesitate, and the brass limb does not tire. Progress is measured one cog at a time.” — The Gear-Father

illustrations.caption: “The escapement heart does not hesitate, and the brass limb does not tire. Progress is measured one cog at a time.” — The Gear-Father

kethrin.tooltipSummary: Retrofuturistic artisan engineers adorned with exposed ticking gears, brass dials, and diving-suit goggles, channeling machine-songs through intricate mechanical prosthetics.
kethrin.description: The Brasskin are retrofuturistic artisan engineers born into the corporate guild system, inheritors of formal training, ancient proprietary oral traditions, and the proud aesthetic of exposed, precision-machined brass. Heavily influenced by an industrial diving-suit and art-deco workshop aesthetic, they wear heavy brass diving-suit goggles with swiveling magnifying loupes, analog needle pressure gauges, and chest-mounted pressure regulators. Their beards are meticulously braided with copper wire, gear-teeth, and fiber-optic strands. Every Brasskin sports visible mechanical prosthetics—articulated brass arms with pneumatic piston joints, exposed escapement ratchets, or whirring clockwork tickers in their chest cavities—awarded by guild syndicates as both trade credential and status symbol. Their hands are precise. Their minds are methodical. The Guild-Bound Brasskin trace their lineage to Brasskin Gear-Father, who founded the first holdfast eight millennia before the Freezing Era, maintaining oral maintenance songs that are the oldest continuous knowledge transmission in the known world.
kethrin.culturalBackground:
Brasskin culture is built on intellectual property preservation. They maintain the old songs exactly as they were taught, follow security protocols without deviation, and believe the Fex's survival depends on guarding what remains of the original knowledge. They are not wrong. The oral traditions are the only record of how the oldest machines function, and every deviation introduces error, and errors compound over millennia. A Brasskin who innovates is a Brasskin who has admitted the old ways are insufficient, and that admission is the first crack in the foundation of guild authority.

Guild hierarchy is rigid and hereditary. Children are apprenticed to their parents' guild syndicate at age five. Promotion is slow, based on demonstrated mastery and political patience. A Brasskin elder has spent two centuries accumulating the copper wires and gear-teeth in their beard, and they do not share hard-won blueprints with juniors who have not yet earned it. The Craft-Hoarding is not cruelty. It is corporate tradition. A technique shared too freely loses value. A formula given without proper apprenticeship is a formula wasted.

Kethrin dominate the holdfast councils, control access to the best machine-tending positions, and speak for the Fex in what little trade occurs with the surface. They view the Clan-Free with a mixture of pity and contempt, untrained, undisciplined, unpredictable. They do not see that the Clan-Free are fixing machines the Guilds have already written off as lost.
kethrin.currentCrisis: The First Turbine is dying. The oldest machine in the oldest holdfast, the one that has been running since before speech was invented, has begun emitting a grinding harmonic that vibrates through the entire geothermal grid. The Brasskin guild councils have quarantined the turbine chamber and forbidden discussion, but the harmonic is spreading through the pipes. Every holdfast feels it now. The Guild-Bound are hoarding their maintenance songs tighter than ever, convinced that revealing the full scope of the failure would trigger a panic that could collapse Fex civilization. The older Brasskin know the songs are incomplete. The younger Brasskin know the elders are hiding something. Neither generation trusts the other enough to share what they know, and the turbine's song is getting louder.

traits.name: Machine-Song
traits.description: You sing the old maintenance song for the machine before you, a verse passed down through your guild for millennia, its syllables worn smooth by repetition, its meaning half-forgotten but its power intact. The machine responds. For 1 minute, one mechanical device, construct, or trap within 30 feet operates at peak efficiency: constructs gain +10ft speed, mechanical devices function perfectly regardless of damage, and traps gain +2 to their save DC. The song requires your voice uninterrupted, if you are silenced, the effect ends. When the song ends, the machine has been pushed past its limits: it takes 2d6 damage as the strain of perfect operation catches up. You cannot sing the same song to the same machine again until after a long rest, the machine needs time to recover from being reminded of what it once was.

effects.name: Peak Operation
effects.description: One construct or mechanical device operates at peak: +10ft speed, traps +2 DC. Duration: 1 minute or until silenced.

statusEffect.description: The machine remembers what it once was

effects.name: Overstrain
effects.description: When the song ends, the machine takes 2d6 damage from the strain. Cannot sing to the same machine again until long rest.

traits.name: Guild Precision
traits.description: Advantage on all checks to repair, disable, or modify mechanical devices and traps; when you spend at least 1 minute on a task that normally takes 1 action, treat any roll of 9 or lower as a 10. You suffer disadvantage on initiative rolls; precision is not speed. (The muscle memory of your guild lives in your fingers, four thousand years deep, and those hands have not fumbled in millennia.)

effects.name: Guild Training
effects.description: Advantage on checks to repair, disable, or modify mechanical devices and traps. When spending 1 minute on a 1-action task, treat rolls of 9 or lower as 10.

statusEffect.description: Your hands remember what your mind has forgotten

effects.name: Deliberate Pace

traits.name: Hoarded Secret
traits.description: Once per long rest, when you or an ally within 30 feet fails a check to repair, disable, or understand a mechanical device, trap, or construct, you may use your reaction to make that check succeed instead. Any Guild-Bound Fex who hears you knows you shared guild knowledge outside the guild, and you cannot use this again for 24 hours. (The half-remembered syllables are older than the current tongue; the machine obeys, but the guild remembers everything.)

effects.name: Guild Secret
effects.description: Once per long rest, reaction to turn a failed mechanical check within 30ft into a success. The secret is spoken, other Brasskin will know you shared it.

statusEffect.description: The old syllables leave your mouth; the machine obeys. But the guild remembers everything.

effects.name: The Guild Remembers
effects.description: Any Guild-Bound Fex who heard you knows you shared guild knowledge. Social consequences at GM discretion. Cannot use again for 24 hours.

statusEffect.description: +1 AP gained instantly from overclocked graft.

effects.name: Frame Overheat

drall.tooltipSummary: Mad-scientist sump alchemists combining botanical greenhouse alembics, fungal distillations, and volatile mineral tinctures inside BioShock-style rubberized suits and brass respirators.
drall.description: The Alchemite are Clan-Free survivors who combine volatile industrial chemistry with earthy, subterranean botanical and fungal distillation. Embracing a mad-scientist BioShock flair, they outfit themselves in heavy vulcanized rubber suits, lead-lined aprons, and archaic brass respirators with twin ribbed rubber hoses and circular glass portholes. Rather than adopting rigid mechanical clockwork, they harvest alchemical runoff, phosphorescent cave mosses, and giant shelf-fungi to brew volatile acids, herbal tinctures, and revitalizing nerve-salts. Their cybernetic replacements are custom-built alchemical grafts: chemical-injectors, pressurized glass retorts, and copper-valve distribution lines integrated directly into their bodies. They live in the deep sump-tunnels, salvaging the chemical runoffs discarded by the corporate holdfasts above and transforming toxic waste into subterranean life.
drall.culturalBackground: Alchemite culture is built on survival chemistry, subterranean botany, and alchemical rebellion. They do not have the luxury of proprietary blueprints; they have greenhouse alembics, bubbling retorts, glowing copper pipes, and terrariums cultivating phosphorescent lichen and spore-fungi. A Alchemite workshop is a chaotic laboratory filled with glass flasks, coils of rubber siphon tubing, acid-stained slate tables, and hand-etched copper syringe kits. They share botanical formulas freely, knowing that a single block in a ventilation line or a contaminated water filter could wipe out an entire community. They barter their medicinal tinctures, acid flasks, glow-lamps, and deep-cavern chemical components in the Sump-Markets in exchange for guild-made hardware. The Clan-Free Alchemite swelled in numbers during the Contraction (Years 200-450) as failing geothermal systems collapsed holdfasts and forced Fex out of the guild system. The Alchemite have been the Fex diaspora's improvising majority for over 400 years.
drall.currentCrisis: The Sump-Markets are flooding, not with water, with Brasskin. As the guild system tightens its information lockdown around the dying turbines, disillusioned apprentices, disgraced journeymen, and expelled guild members descend into the sump-tunnels seeking Clan-Free shelter. The Alchemite were never designed to absorb this many refugees. Their salvage-based economy is straining beyond capacity. Their improvisational repair techniques, never tested at industrial scale, are being asked to keep critical infrastructure running. And whispered rumors from the deepest sump-levels suggest that the Deep Alchemists, the same faction that created the Groven, have begun offering sanctuary to Alchemite exiles in exchange for test subjects. The Alchemite must decide whether to absorb the guild refugees, turn them away, or ally with the one faction every Fex has sworn never to trust again.

traits.name: Jury-Rig
traits.description: You can bypass guild-protocols and make a broken machine run on spit and spite. Once per short rest, you can restore 1d10 HP to a damaged mechanical device, construct, or trap within 5 feet. If the device was inactive, it boots up instantly. But this is a jury-rig, not a guild repair: after 10 minutes, the machine shorts out, taking 2d10 ember damage as the improvised connections melt. You cannot jury-rig the same machine again until it is fully repaired by normal means.

effects.name: Jury-Rigged
effects.description: Restore 1d10 HP to construct/device. Device works for 10 minutes, then takes 2d10 ember damage and breaks.

statusEffect.description: Improvised power courses through the joints

traits.name: Sump-Acclimation

In clean surface air, your speed is reduced by 5 feet as your scarred lungs struggle with pure oxygen. (You breathed the sump's heavy-metal exhaust so long your quicksilver blood now neutralizes the poison, but it never learned to breathe clean.)

effects.name: Sump-Immunity
effects.description: Immune to blight damage and the poisoned condition. Advantage on disease saves.

statusEffect.description: Your quicksilver blood neutralizes heavy metals

effects.name: Clean Air Asthma
effects.description: -5ft speed in clean surface air. Your scarred lungs struggle with pure oxygen.

traits.name: Sump-Salvage

You cannot harvest the same device twice, and you must have your hands free to grab the parts as they fall. (Your mechanical replacement was built from trash, and you never stopped treating destruction as a supply run.)

florae.cardFlavor: The erased 7th noble house (House Viridane) transformed by ancient forest pacts into tree-born treant-kin with crude branch-arms, water dependency, and twig-regrowth.
florae.visualDescription: Standing 5'4" to 6'4" with friendly, carved-wooden faces, expressive amber eyes, and wide warm smiles. Their arms are crude, natural tree boughs (oak, birch, willow, pine, or rowan) that split into flexible twig-fingers sprouting fresh green leaf-buds when hydrated. Small forest creatures (squirrels, bluebirds, owls) often perch on their shoulder-boughs. They wear high-collared traveler coats with blank unstitched Viridane crest patches and copper water-flasks on their belts. Some groom themselves neatly ('Pruned') to travel in cities, while others remain unkempt and leaf-covered ('Wild') in the deep groves.
florae.description:
**[The Tree-Born Exiles of House Viridane]**, *In a sunlit pine grove, a friendly Florae ranger with gnarled oak branch-arms shares a berry with a red squirrel perched on his shoulder bough, his copper water-flask gleaming at his belt.*

House Viridane was one of the seven original public binding houses. During the Years of Whispers it refused Keth's false summons and accepted refuge from the distinct native Unnamed Green. Its people survived as Florae, while their new covenant ended the original public Aex obligation. Morrath received the political seat, not an intact replacement seal. The separate Unwritten family maintains the Secret Aegis.

While the other families heard Keth Amar's whispers and prepared their children for the peaks, House Viridane heard a different voice, something watching from the mist, older than the Sun-Eater's hunger. It reached them before Keth Amar could, offering a way that did not end with their children's blood on northern stone. They took it. They fled south through the Frostwood Reach while the sacrifice fires still burned for the other houses.

In the moonlit groves, starving and hunted, they fulfilled an ancient nature contract with the forest powers. In exchange for protection, their flesh was woven into living timber, transforming them into the Florae: charming, resilient treant-kin whose crude branch-arms, leafy crowns, and sap-filled veins carry the living proof of a lineage the world pretends never existed.
florae.epicHistory:
Florae oral history preserves Viridane's refusal during the Years of Whispers. The Unnamed Green rescued the family through transformation and erasure; the Sleeping Soul did not personally intervene. Their new covenant saved the people while ending the original public seal. Morrath's political replacement and false pedigree did not restore that obligation. Viridane is distinct from the hidden Unwritten family and carries no secret seventh cleansing key.

While the other families heard Keth Amar's whispers and prepared their children for the peaks, House Viridane heard a different voice, something watching from the mist, older than the Sun-Eater's hunger. It reached them before Keth Amar could, offering a way that did not end with their children's blood on northern stone. They took it. They fled south through the Frostwood Reach while the sacrifice fires still burned for the other houses.

In the moonlit groves, starving and hunted, they fulfilled an ancient nature contract with the forest powers. In exchange for protection, their flesh was woven into living timber, transforming them into the Florae: charming, resilient treant-kin whose crude branch-arms, leafy crowns, and sap-filled veins carry the living proof of a lineage the world pretends never existed.
florae.overview:
The Florae are the transformed descendants of House Viridane, a people deeply attuned to nature like druids. Their arms are crude, natural tree boughs — oak, birch, willow, pine, or mountain rowan — that split into flexible twig-fingers that sprout fresh green leaves when hydrated. Small woodland creatures like squirrels, bluebirds, and chipmunks are naturally drawn to them, often nesting in their shoulder boughs.

They depend on fresh water to keep their timber limbs limber. A Florae carries a copper Hearth-Water Flask on their belt as their prized possession. When well-watered, their leaves bloom and their twig-fingers regrow quickly if damaged. If scorched by fire, their outer bark chars into smoldering embers — granting them temporary burning melee strikes, but making them desperate to douse themselves in water.

They do not write their history on paper; ink cannot hold their truth. Instead, they pass their past aloud, elder to child, carrying their identity in spoken chants and negative-space clothing. Every Florae coat features a blank rectangular patch where their noble house crest was unstitched after the world erased them.
quickFacts: The transformed descendants of House Viridane, the 7th noble house that refused Keth Amar's bargain and made an ancient fae-nature pact in the fog-shrouded groves.

Their arms are crude, natural tree boughs (oak, birch, willow, pine) that sprout leaves when hydrated and regrow twigs over time. Small forest animals (squirrels, songbirds) naturally nest on their shoulders.

Play a Florae to be a charming, nature-bound treant-kin adventurer. You carry a copper water-flask to keep your branches limber, resist physical harm through timber hide, and carry the weight of a house the world tried to erase.
florae.culturalBackground:
Florae society is dedicated to tending trees and nurturing the forest. Oaken settlements are rooted firmly on the forest ground floor — cozy timber dwellings carved into titanic buttress roots and hollowed lower trunks of ancient trees, connected by mossy earthen avenues, shaded root-arches, and clear rain basins. Briaren settlements, by contrast, feature beautifully organized botanical architecture: towering thistle spires ringed by sculpted briar hedges, manicured arches, and fragrant blooming roses.

Oaken younglings emerge from Sapling-Sprouts planted in sacred ground nurseries, watered and taught oral history by their elders. Briaren are biologically born to thorn-blooded parents, with permanent contract-barbs emerging at adolescence. Both grow and mature; neither carries every ancestor's personal memories automatically.

Whether a Florae appears 'Wild' (unkempt with leafy crowns and mossy shoulders in deep groves) or 'Pruned' (groomed and manicured under high-collared traveler coats in human cities) is a matter of personal choice and lifestyle. Both carry the same warm heartwood core, the same copper water-flask, and the same blank unstitched Viridane crest patch.
florae.variantDiversity: The Florae split into two subraces born of the same fae-contract. The Briaren paid the contract's price in thorns: their forearms bristle with living barbs, and they dwell in towns of exquisitely organized botanical architecture featuring sculpted thistle hedges, blooming roses, and manicured briar arches around soaring spires. The Oaken paid the price in timber: their arms are crude branch-boughs of oak, birch, willow, pine, or rowan, and they live exclusively on the forest ground floor among titanic buttress roots, hollowed lower trunks, and mossy earthen avenues. Both subraces choose a personal lifestyle of Wild (unkempt, leafy) or Pruned (neatly groomed, high-collared) regardless of their bloodline.

integrationNotes.actionPointSystem: Florae abilities focus on timber resilience, twig regrowth, water-based recovery, and nature-communion. Their branch-arms provide natural melee reach and grapples.
integrationNotes.backgroundSynergy: Florae excel in backgrounds emphasizing survival, nature, herbalism, and guardianship. Their druidic connection creates rich roleplay hooks with woodland creatures and ancient groves.
integrationNotes.classCompatibility: The Briaren carry the lunar parasite as their blood inheritance, so the Lunarch is native to them; they are also native to the Animist (thorn-cantor for the Unwritten dead) and Toxicologist (thorn-sap distillations). Oaken Florae, the tree-born house that passes in cities, are native to the Toxicologist (grove chemistry), the Animist (grove-litany carried in splinter-grafts), and the Lunarch (containing the parasite through timber restraint). Other paths are acquired, never native.

viridian.visualDescription: Standing 5'6" to 6'2" with lean, fae-slender builds and forearms that bristle with living thorn-barbs grown from beneath the skin. Their eyes shift to the green of deep canopy, and their hair often weaves itself into briar-tangles if left uncombed. They wear thorn-cloaks openly in the deep groves and high-collared traveler coats (with the unstitched Viridane crest patch) when they must pass through Ledgered towns. Small forest creatures give them a wide berth; the thorns mark them, and the barbs carry the old fae-contract in their flesh.
viridian.tooltipSummary: Thorn-blooded Florae whose forearms bristle with the living barbs of the old fae-contract, carrying the Unwritten Word and the refusal of the Fog Compact.
viridian.description:
The Briaren are the Briaren Florae, the ones who kept House Viridane's refusal in their flesh. When the fae-contract was struck in the moonlit groves, the price came due two ways: thorns for the Briaren, timber for the Oaken. The Briaren grew barbs from their forearms that mark them as the physical embodiment of the pact, and they retreated into the deepest ironwood groves to tend the places where the uncorrupted Monolith fragment was hidden.

They reject the Fog Compact entirely. Where House Thalreth traded the Frostwood Reach's clarity for insulating mist, the Briaren believe the fog itself is the enemy, slowly erasing everything that made the forest sacred. The cleansing key carried in House Viridane's blood runs in theirs, and they carry the Unwritten Word, a truth-sense that hears a spoken lie the way a foot feels a false step. The Thorn-Speaker is the voice they elected to speak for them, and every word that one says is a thorn.
viridian.culturalBackground:
Briaren society clusters around bastions of beautifully organized botanical architecture, such as Thornhollow. Rather than wild overgrowth, their towns are shaped with exquisite horticultural precision: soaring central thistle spires surrounded by sculpted thorn hedges, manicured briar arches, blooming climbing roses, and geometric vine-trellis promenades. Young Briaren are not planted like Oaken Sapling-Sprouts; they are born biologically to thorn-blooded parents, and the barbs erupt through the skin in adolescence as the contract asserts itself.

Their oral tradition is fierce and short-spoken. They keep the names of every house that broke the Great Binding, every house that marched its firstborn north, and they sing them only as warnings. A Briaren who leaves the deep groves does so as a partisan, carrying the refusal into the Ledgered world at great personal cost. The fog erodes them faster than it erodes the Oaken, and they know it.

baseTraits.reproduction: Biological birth; contract-barbs emerge at adolescence

traits.name: Thorn-Barb Bristle

traits.name: The Unwritten Word

You have advantage on Insight checks to detect spoken lies, and you cannot be deceived by mundane falsehoods spoken aloud in your presence. The cost of this gift is symmetric: you have disadvantage on Deception checks to speak a direct verbal lie, though you may still mislead by omission, misdirection, or carefully chosen truths.

effects.name: Truth-Sense
effects.description: Advantage on Insight vs spoken lies; mundane verbal falsehoods detected automatically.
effects.mechanicsText: Advantage on Insight checks to detect lies; auto-detect mundane spoken deception.

effects.name: Truth-Bound
effects.description: Disadvantage on Deception checks to speak a direct verbal lie.
effects.mechanicsText: Disadvantage on Deception to tell a spoken falsehood.

traits.name: Fog-Compact Refusal

The recorded +2 difficulty for interrogation or magical extraction represents the refusal, not automatic preservation of every ancestor's personal memories.

effects.mechanicsText: Advantage on saves vs memory-altering and fog-based effects.

oken.description:
The Oaken are the tree-born Florae, the ones whose flesh was woven into living timber when the fae-contract was struck. Where the Briaren grew thorns, the Oaken grew wood: crude branch-arms of oak, birch, willow, pine, or rowan that split into flexible twig-fingers sprouting fresh leaf-buds when hydrated, and sap-filled veins where the Briaren carry barbs.

The Oaken did not refuse the Fog Compact; they endure it. Where the Briaren retreated into the deep groves to keep the refusal alive, the Oaken moved through the Ledgered towns, pruning themselves neat and walking under high-collared coats with the unstitched Viridane crest patch at the breast. A Pruned Oaken can pass in Drunhold or Greymark Keep long enough to trade; a Wild Oaken stays in the ground-floor root-hollow sanctuaries where the Sapling-Sprouts are planted in rich forest loam and sung into shape by elders with copper water-flasks at their belts.
oken.culturalBackground:
Oaken society is dedicated to tending trees and nurturing the forest from the ground up. Their homes are built strictly on the forest ground floor — cozy timber dwellings carved directly into titanic buttress roots and hollowed base trunks of colossal ancient trees, connected by mossy earthen avenues, shaded root-arches, and clear rain basins (strictly no treetop or canopy living).

Oaken younglings are not born biologically; they are planted. Every youngling begins as a Sapling-Sprout planted in a sacred forest nursery bed of rich mossy loam on the forest floor. The elders water them daily with fresh rainwater, share berries with visiting squirrels, and sing the oral history until the saplings grow their first crude branch-arms and step out of the soil as young Oaken.

Whether an Oaken appears 'Wild' (unkempt with leafy crowns and mossy shoulders in deep groves) or 'Pruned' (groomed and manicured under high-collared traveler coats in human cities) is a matter of personal choice and lifestyle. Both carry the same warm heartwood core, the same copper water-flask, and the same blank unstitched Viridane crest patch.

traits.name: Heartwood Density
traits.description: Your trunk and limbs are forged from dense living timber (oak, birch, or rowan) instead of soft flesh. You gain +1 Durability (flat reduction against all physical damage). However, this ancient timber density reduces your base movement speed by 5 feet.

effects.name: Heartwood Core
effects.description: +1 Durability (flat physical damage reduction); -5 ft movement speed.
effects.mechanicsText: Gain +1 Durability against physical damage; base speed reduced by 5 ft.

effects.name: Dense Timber Strides
effects.description: -5 ft base movement speed.
effects.mechanicsText: Base movement speed reduced by 5 ft.

traits.name: Canopy-Weaver Reach
traits.description: Your crude branch-arms flex and extend with druidic fluidity. You gain a +20 ft climbing speed, +5 feet of reach on melee attacks and touch interactions, and advantage on Athletics and Acrobatics checks made to traverse forest canopy or wooden architecture.

effects.name: Extended Bough
effects.description: +5 ft melee reach, +20 ft climb speed, advantage on canopy traversal.
effects.mechanicsText: +5 ft melee reach and +20 ft climb speed.

traits.name: Deep-Root Anchor
traits.description: Once per short rest as an Action (1 AP), sink your branch-feet into soil, moss, or fractured stone for up to 1 minute. While rooted, your movement speed is 0, but you are immune to prone and forced movement, and you gain +2 DR (Damage Reduction) against all attacks. You may uproot as a free action.

effects.name: Rooted Bulwark
effects.description: +2 DR, immunity to prone and forced movement, movement speed 0.
effects.mechanicsText: Gain +2 DR and immunity to forced movement/prone; movement is 0 while rooted.

groven.name: Groven
groven.essence: The Living Bridges of Cragjaw Peaks
groven.illustrationCaption: “Spanning the chasm where the mountain winds scream, Bridge-Peak anchors our clans above the clouds.” — Span-Master of the High Crag

illustrations.caption: “Spanning the chasm where the mountain winds scream, Bridge-Peak anchors our clans above the clouds.” — Span-Master of the High Crag
“In the deep heat of Morgh-Deep, we bake the clay and temper the bedrock until the mountain itself yields to our hands.” — Kiln-Master of the Vat
“None cross into the high pass without weighing iron against stone. Pay the toll, or test the wind.” — Gate-Warden of Frostmaw
“The gates of Karst-Morgh were not built to keep enemies out, but to remind them of the mountain’s crushing weight.” — Bastion Mason
“A fracture is not an ending; it is where the stone learned how to bend without falling.” — Vorr-Geth the Shattered One

groven.cardFlavor: Once monumental living landmarks, their bodies were engineered by Fex alchemists who reshaped their stone forms to break their bond to the earth.
groven.visualDescription: The Groven are a markedly variable people, divided by lineage into two distinct stone-hewn anatomies. The Morgh are massive, monolithic, primal stone ogre-like humanoids standing 1.50m-1.60m (4'11"-5'3") with enormous boulder-like chests, column-like limbs, rough cracked granite stone-skin, lichen patches, and deep-set glowing amber eyes beneath heavy craggy brow ridges. The Amordjin are tall, athletic mountain stone-trolls standing 2.00m-2.18m (6'7"-7'2") with sweeping backward-curving stone horns along their crown, long braided dreadlocks bound with silver wire and beads, pointed ears with silver hoops, fierce chiseled stone features with prominent lower under-fangs, fine stone-scale plating across their shoulders, and agile limbs with clawed stone hands and feet engineered for navigating high alpine suspension bridges. Both lineages carry long braided hair adorned with silver wire and stone beads. Morgh Groven embody immovable earth-hewn bedrock, while Amordjin Groven dwell along high alpine hillsides and monumental suspension bridges as span-engineers and toll-keepers.
groven.description:
**[The Living Bridges]**, *Standing atop a monumental grand suspension bridge spanning alpine summits, a tall, horned slate-blue Amordjin diplomat weighs coin-tolls on a brass balance scale while terraced hillside dwellings line the mountain slopes below.*

The Groven are the children of the vats and the crags, forged from ancient Thrumm. The Morgh answered their liberation by carving cyclopean subterranean quarry-halls and peak-fastnesses as primal stone ogre artisans, while the Amordjin built monumental mountain suspension bridges and terraced hillside towns, governing commerce across alpine passes.
groven.overview: The Groven are stone-hewn humanoids indigenous to the snow-choked Cragjaw Peaks. Descended from the Thrumm and alchemically liberated from Fex servitude, the Morgh became primal, bulky stone ogre quarry-masons who carve cyclopean subterranean halls and peak-fastnesses, while the Amordjin evolved into tall, athletic, horned stone-trolls with slate-blue mineral skin, sweeping crown horns, dreadlocks, and under-fangs who dwell along terraced mountain hillsides and monumental suspension bridges, governing trade across the peaks.
quickFacts: Stone-hewn humanoids of the Cragjaw Peaks, divided into bulky primal stone ogre Morgh quarry-masons and athletic, horned slate-blue Amordjin bridge-architects.
Amordjin build monumental suspension bridges and terraced hillside aeries, governing alpine trade passes with balance scales.
Play a Groven to explore the legacy of a manufactured race: Amordjin engineering soaring mountain spans and hillside towns, and Morgh tending cyclopean subterranean halls and anvil hearths.
groven.culturalBackground: Groven society is suspended in the vertical world of the Cragjaw Peaks. The Morgh inhabit cyclopean stone halls and subterranean vat-citadels carved deep into the high mountain peaks, vast geothermal-warmed cavern-halls where entire clans live, forge, and tend the Ancestor-Spans that anchor their fastnesses against whiteout blizzards. The Amordjin master monumental bridge-and-mountain architecture: spanning alpine peaks with grand suspension bridges, while families dwell in terraced stone homes carved along the mountain hillsides and cliffs. In Amordjin markets, trade is negotiated with stone-bead ledgers and brass balance scales; in Morgh halls, the old stone-deep customs endure in lichen-fiber knot-records and the slow rhythm of forge and cable.
groven.variantDiversity: The Groven are divided into two primary lineages: the Morgh Groven (primal, bulky stone ogre-like beings and monolithic quarry-masons with cracked granite skin, massive craggy chests, and glowing molten amber eyes, carving cyclopean mountain halls and peak-fastnesses) and the Amordjin Groven (tall, athletic, horned stone-trolls with wind-polished slate-blue mineral skin, sweeping crown horns, dreadlocks with silver wire, pointed ears, prominent lower under-fangs, fine shoulder scales, and clawed climbing limbs, who construct monumental suspension bridges and dwell along terraced alpine mountain hillsides).

integrationNotes.actionPointSystem: Groven abilities emphasize bridge-craft, stone resilience, long-limbed reach, and the spiritual legacy of the Still-Claiming. Their troll-kin heritage balances physical endurance with predatory agility.
integrationNotes.backgroundSynergy: Groven excel in backgrounds emphasizing high mountain survival, bridge-tending, toll-negotiation, stone-lichen weaving, and Fex trade diplomacy.
integrationNotes.classCompatibility: The Morgh and Amordjin are the people who took the alchemists' tools and made them a choice. Both are native to the Shaper (Torin's decision in a collapsing tunnel), to the Warden (the chosen chain), and to the Martyr as the Transmuted Burden — the Morgh anchor the line, the Amordjin span it. The Morgh are also native to the Berserker (Bloodhammer and Toll-war serum overclock), the Amordjin to the Chronarch (bridge-negotiation probability). No other people is native to these paths.
integrationNotes.fexricFriction: Groven-Fex relations are a coiled spring of hatred and denial. Groven view the Fex as butchers who stole their ancestors' stone-heritage to breed them as mining tools, and they guard the Ancestor-Spans with specialized tolls targeting Fex caravans. Fex view Groven as runaway alchemical property that escaped the holdfasts. Yet, they are locked in a symbiotic crisis: Fex need Groven spans to transport geothermal coal, while Groven need Fex metalware to reinforce their bridges. This tension is a constant spark in the Cragjaw Peaks.

groven.diasporaVariation: Groven diaspora follows the Ancestor-Spans and the mercenary trade. Morgh Groven bridge-engineers work the Sundrift Vale crossing-points (heavier-built, heat-stressed, their stone-scale cracking in the dry steppe sun); Amordjin Groven diplomat-mercenaries serve in every regional court as bodyguards and span-advisors. A sea-serving Amordjin (a Groven who has served three generations aboard Iceheart ships) develops webless paddle-hands and a salt-weathered hide, and speaks Fex with a Merryn accent. Frostmaw remains the cultural heart; the diaspora measures its distance from it in generations of bone-knowledge lost.
groven.meaningfulTradeoffs: Groven possess stone-scale plating and superior climbing reach, but their mineral hide betrays them to flame, their long limbs leave defensive gaps, and their bodies sink in deep water, the stone that protects them also drags them down.

baseTraits.build: Markedly variable by caste: stocky, broad, stone-hewn Morgh hall-builders, and tall, slender, span-limbed Amordjin diplomats

groven.epicHistory:
Long before the sun was stolen, before Emberspire erupted and bled volcanic fury into a dying world, the Cragjaw Peaks belonged to the Thrumm, hulking, hunched, primordial stone-trolls of minimal speech and brutish, animal instinct who dwelled in the deepest geothermal warrens, eating what they killed and knowing nothing of tools or trade or the fragile, frantic industry of younger races. They were the mountain's first children, its sovereign inhabitants, and the mountain was warm then, its vents breathing freely through uncounted, silent millennia of solitude and stone.

Native Fex settlement came after the Thrumm's presence in Cragjaw. Their engineering around Vurath preceded the celestial Star-Fall; they were not a newly created freeze-era people. Later Deep Alchemist experiments captured Thrumm broodlings and reshaped them into Groven servitors. The vats, escape, Still-Claiming and voluntary reclamation schools are distinct stages, not one universal celestial bargain.

They captured Thrumm broodlings, young enough that their stone-hide had not fully hardened, their minds not fully set in the old, slow instincts born of eons in the dark. They submerged them in alchemical vats bubbling with serums of their own design: formulas to thin the primordial stone-growth into fine, tessellated scales, to stretch the limbs into long, reaching spans for mining shafts, to stimulate the dormant centers of higher cognition slumbering in the brute troll brain. The experiment was meant to create intelligent servitors, creatures that could both labor in the suffocating dark of the deep mines and interface with Fex machinery. They were bred for obedience, for utility, for the quiet, unquestioning resilience of a tool that does not ask why it was made.

The experiment succeeded in every way except obedience.

The first generation of transformed Thrumm developed will. Then language, crude, halting words that their captors mistook for mimicry. Then dexterity in those long, stretched fingers. Then rage, a cold, gathering fury born of vats and needles and the faces of alchemists peering through glass. They called themselves the Groven, a word that, in the old Thrumm tongue, meant nothing at all, a new sound for a new people, a name chosen rather than assigned. Their strongest, a broodling whose vat-tag read Subject Len-7, was the first to raise a stone-knuckled fist and shatter the glass. The Vat-Breakers, bloodied, slick with alchemical fluid, their new intelligence burning with the clarity of vengeance, freed their kin, slaughtered their captors, and fled upward into the crags where Fex gears could not follow and Fex revenge could not reach. But in the chaos and the screaming and the shattering of glass, dozens of Thrumm broodlings, the Lost Brood, were left behind in the deeper vats, beyond the Vat-Breakers' reach. The Deep Alchemists, shaken but undeterred, tightened security and moved their operations into tunnels so deep the Groven could never find them. The debt has never been repaid.

The Groven found their sanctuary in the high crags, a harsh, vertical world of razor ridges and screaming wind-gaps where no flat ground existed but what they built with their own hands and their own bones. They grew their civilization upward, not outward, a defiance of gravity and geography alike. They learned to weave stone-lichen fiber into bridge-cables stronger than iron, a craft born of necessity and elevated to art. They learned to domesticate the cliff-rams whose wool and meat and rendered tallow sustained them through the long, grinding grey of the perpetual winter. And they discovered the Still-Claiming, the slow, beautiful, terrible process by which a Groven's body, upon death, calcifies into permanent stone, fusing to whatever surface they fell upon with the final, absolute commitment of a people who have always known that the mountain takes back what it gave. The eldest Groven, feeling death approach in the ache of their scales and the slowing of their hearts, began walking to the chasms and letting the calcification take them there, their bodies becoming the first Ancestor-Spans, bridges of bone and mineral and the will to connect what was never meant to be connected.

When the sun was stolen and the world froze, when Emberspire erupted and the noble families sealed their desperate, bloody bargains with the Keth Amar, the family that ruled the Cragjaw Peaks made their own terrible trade. They asked for the eternal snow to hide them, a perpetual, howling blizzard that would cloak the mountains in impenetrable white, bury every pass, swallow every starving horde that sought shelter in their keeps. Keth Amar obliged with the cold, indifferent precision of a thing that has always understood bargains better than mercy. The snow never stopped. Every natural landmark, every ancient trail, every surface route was buried under centuries of grinding, accumulating drift. The keeps survived because nothing could find them. The price, the inescapable, bitter cost of all of Keth Amar's bargains, was that nothing could find anything at all. The Cragjaw Peaks became a white, silent tomb for anyone who did not know the spans.

The Groven bridges, strung above the blizzard line, dark against the endless grey sky, the only visible shape in a world erased by winter, became the sole route through the mountains. Caravans that once crossed by a dozen paths now crossed by one: the Ancestor-Spans, grown from the willing dead, spanning chasms that had swallowed armies and expeditions and entire civilizations. The Groven began charging tolls. It was not greed, not avarice, not the petty extortion of toll-keepers fattening on desperate travelers. Without the spans, crossing the Cragjaw Peaks was death by exposure and disorientation and the slow, grinding hunger of the blizzard. The toll was the price of survival, and the Groven, patient, pragmatic, forever suspended between the ancient Thrumm they once were and the Fex servitors they refused to become, became the gatekeepers of every pass between the frozen, bitter north and the volcanic, ash-choked south.

As generations passed in the cold grey light of the high crags, the ideological split between the Morgh and the Amordjin hardened into the dominant division of Groven society. It was never a hierarchy of blood. It was the slow crystallization of two answers to the only question that mattered: what does a freed tool become? The Morgh answered with the body: the tool that outlives its purpose becomes the purpose, and they became the bridge: laborers, warriors, and bridge-builders whose hands held cables because the hand, to them, was the cable's purpose. The Amordjin answered with the claim: we built the bridge, the bridge is ours, and they became the owners: diplomats, toll-keepers, and council-speakers whose voices carried in the Stone-Moots because the voice, to them, was the deed of ownership. Their heavier and finer scales, their longer or shorter limbs, were the outward echo of those inward answers, not the cause of them, though generations of convenience let each side forget this. The split was never declared, never written, never acknowledged in any fiber-cord record or council decree. It was simply how things were, an argument without a name, a wound that the Groven inherited from their makers and never learned to close. A Morgh child absorbed their answer with their first scale-shed. An Amordjin child absorbed theirs with their first toll. Both learned, in the same silence, that some things must never be spoken aloud. The divide sharpened into open friction during the Toll Wars (Years 210-340, Freezing Era), when Amordjin diplomats negotiated the treaties that Morgh bridge-builders died to enforce, each side certain the other had mistaken freedom for something it was not.

The present Groven face failing spans, evidence of continuing vat operations and new shard resonance. A genuine great Aex shard rests in Cragjaw; physical shards are not in one-to-one correspondence with living seals or houses. The Lost Brood remains an unresolved history, while maintained Ancestor-Spans carry the dead's material legacy. Morgh's short, stocky dimensions and Amordjin's taller athletic frame remain distinct; an ogre-like art silhouette does not grant giant-size mechanics.

notableFigures.name: Vorr-Geth, Last of the Vat-Breakers
notableFigures.title: The Shattered One
notableFigures.backstory:
Vorr-Geth is the last living Groven to have shattered a vat with their own hands, the final survivor of the original escape from the Deep Alchemists' laboratories beneath Frostmaw Crag. No one knows exactly how old Vorr-Geth is. The serums that smoothed their flesh also slowed their aging, and the Still-Claiming that should have taken them eighty years ago has instead crept across only their left arm, which is now solid obsidian from shoulder to fingertip.

Vorr-Geth does not sit on the Stone-Moot council. They do not negotiate tolls or tend bridges or offer wisdom to the young. They live alone in a shallow cave facing the deepest chasm in the Cragjaw Peaks, the one the Vat-Breakers crossed during their escape, before there were Ancestor-Spans, before there were bridges at all. Groven of both bloodlines make pilgrimages to Vorr-Geth's cave, leaving offerings of lichen-fiber cord and cliff-ram tallow, hoping for a word from the last living witness to their origin.

Vorr-Geth rarely speaks. When they do, it is about the Lost Brood, the broodlings left behind in the deeper vats, never rescued. Vorr-Geth remembers their faces. The Still-Claiming is taking the rest of Vorr-Geth slowly, deliberately, as if the mountain wants to preserve the last Vat-Breaker as long as possible. When the calcification reaches their heart, Vorr-Geth will become a statue at the mouth of the chasm, the first span, the first witness, the first and final reproach.

notableFigures.name: Ithra-Mal, High Toll-Keeper of Frostmaw Crag
notableFigures.title: The Voice of the Spans
notableFigures.backstory:
Ithra-Mal is the most powerful Amordjin diplomat in living memory, the High Toll-Keeper who negotiates passage rates for every major caravan that crosses the Cragjaw Peaks. Her voice is the voice of the bridge, when she sets a toll, it is binding. When she refuses passage, the caravan turns back or dies in the blizzard.

She was born on the Widest Span, the largest Ancestor-Span in the Cragjaw Peaks, delivered into the wind and the void while a blizzard howled below. Her mother, a fiber-weaver of the bridge-top settlements, wrapped her in lichen-cord and hung the bundle from a span-cable to keep her above the frost while the birth concluded. Ithra-Mal jokes that she learned to negotiate before she learned to breathe, the mountain demanded her life at birth and she talked it down.

Her relationship with the Fex is famously complicated. She negotiates salt and gear-work from the deep tunnel delegations with cold precision, extracting favorable terms that no other Amordjin has matched. But in private, she funds expeditions into the lower tunnels, small teams of Morgh warriors and Murmur-Blooded scouts who search for signs of the Deep Alchemists' current operations. She has never spoken publicly about the Lost Brood. Her office receives regular reports from the tunnel-scouts. The reports are filed in a locked fiber-cord ledger that only she can read.

notableFigures.name: Geth-Run, the Murmur-Blooded
notableFigures.title: The Bridge Between
notableFigures.backstory:
Geth-Run was born with scales too fine for the Morgh warrens but too coarse for the Amordjin bridge-tops, limbs longer than Morgh but shorter than Amordjin, a Murmur-Blood, the rare product of mixed-bloodline parentage. Neither warren accepted them. No elder vouched for their name. The Morgh called them 'half-voiced.' The Amordjin called them 'half-stone.' Both meant the same thing: you do not fully belong.

Geth-Run chose exile rather than a lifetime of straddling a divide that had no place for them. For forty years, they have walked the highest, narrowest Ancestor-Spans, the ones too dangerous for toll-caravans, the ones that Groven society has forgotten. They maintain these spans alone, replacing frayed cables, shoring cracked stone, ensuring that the bridge that no one uses is still there when someone needs it.

Their knowledge of the Cragjaw Peaks is unmatched. They know which spans are dying, which passes have been claimed by the Wyrd, which tunnels the Fex have reopened. Both Morgh and Amordjin consult Geth-Run when they need information no official record holds, and both offer payment in the form of supplies left at a designated span-marker. Geth-Run accepts the supplies and answers the questions but never descends to the warrens or the bridge-towns. The exile was not their choice, but the solitude has become one.

majorLocations.name: Frostmaw Crag
majorLocations.description:
The ancestral heartland of the Groven, a towering peak at the center of the Cragjaw range where the blizzards blow hardest and the geothermal vents still breathe with the mountain's dying warmth. The crag is honeycombed with warrens, bridge-towns, and vertical cliff-villages, all connected by a web of Ancestor-Spans that have been growing for centuries.

At the peak, the Stone-Moot Spire holds the council chamber where Amordjin elders convene to set toll rates, adjudicate disputes, and speak for the spans. The chamber is carved into the living rock and lit by vent-glass lanterns filled with phosphorescent lichen, their pale green glow the only color in the grey stone. No Morgh has ever spoken in this chamber; the Morgh have never sought to, the bridge speaks through the hands, not the voice, and the Amordjin have never insisted otherwise, which is its own kind of enforcement.

At the base, where the crag meets the frozen valleys below, the Root-Halls house the oldest Morgh families, the ones who have tended the same bridge-foundations for generations. These vast stone halls are the deep heart of the Morgh, their walls carved with knotted fiber-cord records of every birth, death, and bridge-tending in the clan's history.

The deep tunnels below Frostmaw Crag lead to the Fex territories and, further still, to the Subterranean Vault where the Sundered Monolith rests, a chamber sealed by Aethil's original contract, where the snow does not fall and the walls have never seen frost. The Groven do not guard the Vault. They simply do not speak of it to outsiders. The mountain keeps its own secrets.

majorLocations.name: The First Span
majorLocations.description:
The oldest Ancestor-Span in the Cragjaw Peaks, grown from the body of the first Vat-Breaker who died in the upper crags after the escape. Her name was lost, the Fex vat-tags were discarded in the flight, and she died before the Groven had invented the knot-record that would preserve memory. All that remains is the span itself: a bridge of fused stone, bone, and mineral that crosses the widest chasm in Frostmaw Crag, suspended a thousand feet above the blizzard floor.

The First Span is sacred but not sacred, the Groven do not worship their dead. They maintain them. A dedicated team of Morgh bridge-tenders lives on the span year-round, replacing cables, monitoring cracks, and recording every shift in the stone. The span has outlasted seventeen generations of tenders. It has survived three earthquakes, two Draskar raids, and one attempt by the Fex to mine its foundation for crystallized bone.

Pilgrims from both bloodlines visit the First Span to leave offerings at the point where the original Vat-Breaker's hands fused to the chasm wall, the first grasp, the first anchor, the moment that proved bridges could be grown instead of built. The offerings are small: a length of fiber-cord, a ram-horn button, a polished obsidian bead. The span remembers them all. The stone beneath the offerings has grown faint impressions of every gift left there, the mountain recording gratitude the way it records death.

majorLocations.name: The Shaping Hall
majorLocations.description: Carved into the warmest geothermal vent of Frostmaw Crag, the Shaping Hall trains those who would reshape their own bodies. It was founded by the Morgh elders after the miner Torin held a collapsing tunnel through alchemical bone-growth during the First Thermal War, coaxing his own stone-scale into load-bearing pillars that kept the passage open long enough for three hundred Groven to reach the deep lifts. The elders spent a generation reverse-engineering the technique, and now any Morgh who proves their resolve may learn to direct the Still-Claiming deliberately, calcifying a limb, reinforcing a ribcage, or growing a fresh span of living stone from an open wound. The Hall is the only place in the Cragjaw Peaks where the Still-Claiming is treated as a craft rather than a death sentence, and its graduates carry the faint mineral smell of warm serums and the deliberate stillness of people who have already decided which part of themselves to sacrifice next.

groven.currentCrisis:
Three crises press upon the Groven in the present age, and none are spoken of openly.

The first is the cracking of the Ancestor-Spans. The Still-Claimed dead who form the bridges are centuries old, and the eternal blizzard that hides the peaks also wears at the stone. The oldest spans are developing fractures that no bridge-tender has been able to seal. The Morgh whisper that the mountain is taking back what it gave, that the Deep Thrum, the mineral consciousness of the Cragjaw Peaks, is slowly dying and can no longer sustain the dead who became its bones. The Amordjin refuse to confirm or deny this. The tolls continue. The spans continue. The fractures continue.

The second is the Lost Brood. The Groven have never repaid the debt of the broodlings left behind in the vats during the Vat-Breakers' escape. For centuries, the Groven told themselves the Lost Brood were certainly dead, that no Thrumm could survive decades of Fex experimentation. But recent expeditions into the lower tunnels have returned with evidence to the contrary: abandoned vat-chambers, fresh alchemical residue, and, in one case, a fragment of stone-scale that was unmistakably Groven, too fine for Thrumm, too recent to be ancient. The Deep Alchemists are still operating. The Lost Brood may still be alive. And the Groven must decide whether to descend, at last, and finish what the Vat-Breakers started, or admit that they have spent centuries rationalizing cowardice as patience.

The third is the Sundered Monolith in the Subterranean Vault. The shard hums louder each year, and the stone around it has begun to grow warm, the first warmth the Vault has known since Keth Amar's bargain was sealed. The Amordjin elders debate what this means in closed council. The Morgh bridge-tenders feel it in their bones: a vibration in the oldest spans, like a heartbeat accelerating. The mountain is changing. Keth Amar's grip on the world is tightening. And the Groven, who have spent centuries tending bridges that span a dying peak, must decide whether their role is to maintain what was built, or to build something new before the old stone fails.
groven.culturalPractices:
Every Groven child is born with the Vat-Sleep, the monthly dream of warm fluid and cold glass and the first scream that never learned to stop echoing. It arrives without warning, silent and inescapable, always the same: the suffocating dark of the alchemical vat, the blurred, distorted shapes of Fex alchemists moving beyond the glass, the moment the serums hit the blood and everything, body, mind, self, is remade into something that was not there before. No Groven has ever been spared this dream. The Morgh call it a reminder of what was taken. The Amordjin call it an inheritance of what was given. Both call it the price of what they are, a monthly tithe paid to an origin they did not choose.

The first shedding of the scales marks a Groven's passage from child to adult, a rite as ancient and inexorable as the mountain itself. Morgh children shed heavily: thick, dark plates of mineral that crack and fall away in heavy shards, revealing new scales beneath, denser and darker still, ready for the grueling, stoic life of the warrens. The shed scales are collected by the child's parents and woven into a sash that the Morgh wears for the rest of their life, a record of growth, a chain of renewal. Amordjin children shed finely: a pale, delicate dusting of mineral flakes that drift away in the wind before they can be caught. The Amordjin do not collect their shed. The wind takes them. The wind remembers. The Amordjin say this is enough.

Every Morgh undergoes the Bridge-Vow upon reaching adulthood: a formal, binding pledge to tend a specific Ancestor-Span for a minimum of twenty years, two decades of wind and cold and the slow, grinding labor of keeping the dead upright. The span is assigned by the warren elders based on need and the young Morgh's demonstrated skill with cable and stone and the patient, wordless endurance that cannot be taught. To refuse the Bridge-Vow is to become vok-morgh, unwilled stone, unshaped mineral, a thing without purpose, and no Morgh who carries that mark will ever be trusted with a span-cable again. The warrens have no punishment worse than irrelevance.

Every Amordjin undergoes the First Toll, a ritual negotiation conducted with an elder Amordjin who plays the role of an outsider caravan-master with the practiced, weary cunning of someone who has haggled for passage across forty different spans. The young Amordjin must set a fair toll and defend it against argument, insult, bribery, and the quiet, insidious appeal to pity. Those who fail the First Toll are not exiled but restricted: they may negotiate for their own clan but never represent the Stone-Moot in external dealings, never speak with the voice of the bridge. The Amordjin say the First Toll is not a test of greed but of judgment, the ability to name a fair price and hold the line when everything in the room is trying to move you. The Morgh say it is a test of exactly what it looks like, and they do not say this kindly.

Death comes for every Groven, and the Still-Claiming follows within hours, a slow, inexorable calcification that begins at the extremities and spreads inward like frost across a window. The stone-scales creep across the cooling flesh, hardening, fusing, committing the corpse to whatever surface it fell upon in an act of permanent, unbreakable kinship with the mountain. Within days, the body is a statue, the face of the dead frozen in their final posture, a monument that will stand until the Cragjaw Peaks themselves erode to dust. The Morgh elderly walk into the chasms when they feel death approaching in the deep ache of their scales, choosing which span will receive their bones with the same deliberation a farmer chooses which field to plant. The Amordjin elderly debate death endlessly, where to fall, what posture to hold, whether the span needs another body or whether a bridge is already complete, whether it is better to become a span or a spire or simply a statue in a council chamber, frozen mid-argument, the point you were making preserved forever in stone.

The toll is sacred. Every outsider who crosses an Ancestor-Span must pay something, coin if they carry it, goods if they have none, a story if they have nothing else, a breath of warmth if the story is insufficient. The Morgh collect the toll with heavy, patient hands. The Amordjin set the rate with the cold, practiced precision of those who know exactly what a bridge is worth because they have spent their lives walking graves. Both halves know, in the unspoken kinship of shared purpose, that the toll is not about wealth. It is about acknowledgment. The bridges were made of Groven dead, calcified, willing, permanent. To cross without paying is to walk over a grave and pretend the body beneath you does not exist. No Groven forgives this. The mountain remembers what the traveler pretends to forget.

sharedTraits.name: Vat-Sleep Disorientation
sharedTraits.description: Vat-Sleep leaves you disoriented after long rests: disadvantage on Initiative in the first combat after a long rest. The alchemical serums that made your people never fully left your blood, and the vat-dream lingers in your limbs for minutes after waking.

effects.name: Vat-Sleep Hangover
effects.description: Disadvantage on Initiative in the first combat after a long rest.
effects.mechanicsText: You roll Initiative with disadvantage in the first combat after a long rest, reflecting lingering disorientation from the Vat-Sleep.

sharedTraits.name: Vat-Sleep
sharedTraits.description: Every Groven carries the Vat-Sleep in their blood, the monthly dream of warm fluid and cold glass, of blurred alchemists peering through their prison, of the first scream that has never stopped echoing through the stone of Frostmaw Crag. The dream arrives without warning, always the same, a tithe paid to an origin no Groven chose. But the serums that shaped you also preserved the memory of your ancestors, the Thrumm who walked the deep crags before the Fex ever arrived. Once per long rest, when you make an Intelligence (History) check related to the Cragjaw Peaks, ancient Thrumm, Groven ancestors, or Fex alchemy, you may roll with advantage as the Vat-Sleep surfaces fragments of ancestral knowledge. When you wake from the Vat-Sleep, you are Disoriented for 10 minutes (-2 to all Perception checks) as the boundary between dream and waking blurs, for those ten minutes, you are still half-submerged in glass.

effects.name: Ancestral Memory
effects.description: Once per long rest, advantage on Intelligence (History) checks related to the Cragjaw Peaks, ancient Thrumm, Groven ancestors, or Fex alchemy.
effects.mechanicsText: Once per long rest, you gain advantage on Intelligence (History) checks about the Cragjaw Peaks, the Thrumm, Groven ancestors, or Fex alchemy.

effects.name: Disoriented
effects.description: -2 to all Perception checks for 10 minutes upon waking from the Vat-Sleep.
effects.mechanicsText: For 10 minutes after waking from the Vat-Sleep, you take a -2 penalty to all Perception checks as the dream's haze lingers.

sharedTraits.name: Still-Claiming
sharedTraits.description: The mountain takes back what it gave. Every Groven knows this, feels it in the gradual stiffening of scales, the slow mineral creep at the joints, the way stone-scales grow thicker with age as the body prepares itself for the final calcification. When you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you may choose to trigger the Still-Claiming early: your body calcifies into a temporary statue of living stone instead of falling Unconscious. While calcified, you are Petrified, immune to all damage but unable to move, speak, or act. Adjacent allies gain Half Cover (+2 DR and +2 Dodge) from your stone form. At the start of your next turn, the calcification cracks and crumbles, and you fall Unconscious at 0 HP (stable). This ability cannot be used again until you complete a long rest, the mountain will not be called lightly, and each premature calcification taxes the body more than the last.

effects.name: Stone Form
effects.description: Your calcified body provides Half Cover (+2 DR and +2 Dodge) to adjacent allies until the start of your next turn.

selectedEffects.name: Calcification
selectedEffects.description: Petrified for 1 round instead of falling Unconscious at 0 HP. Cannot act but immune to damage. Stabilized when calcification ends.

morgh.name: Morgh
morgh.illustrationCaption: “In the deep heat of Morgh-Deep, we bake the clay and temper the bedrock until the mountain itself yields to our hands.” — Kiln-Master of the Vat

illustrations.caption: “In the deep heat of Morgh-Deep, we bake the clay and temper the bedrock until the mountain itself yields to our hands.” — Kiln-Master of the Vat
“The gates of Karst-Morgh were not built to keep enemies out, but to remind them of the mountain’s crushing weight.” — Bastion Mason
“Every chisel stroke awakens the slumbering song sealed inside the bedrock.” — Shaping Hall Artisan
“A fracture is not an ending; it is where the stone learned how to bend without falling.” — Vorr-Geth the Shattered One

morgh.visualDescription: Massive, monolithic, and primal, the Morgh are rock-hewn stone ogre-like humanoids carrying ancient Thrumm blood closest to the surface. Standing 4'11" to 5'3" (1.50m to 1.60m) with immense crag-shoulders, thick pillar-like limbs, and deep chest bulk, they resemble living bedrock. Their faces are flat, square stone-slab features with deep-set glowing molten amber eyes beneath heavy craggy stone brow ridges, and lipless rock mouths with blunt crushing teeth (strictly no orc tusks, no pig snouts). Their stone-hide grows in rough, cracked granite plates and basalt veins across shoulders, spine, and joints, dotted with dried lichen and moss. When a Morgh stands still among high crag boulders, living rock is indistinguishable from the mountain. They wear heavy ox-hide quarry wraps and carry cyclopean stone-chisels, mauls, or long ash staves.
morgh.tooltipSummary: Massive, primal stone ogre quarry-masons and hall-builders (1.50m-1.60m) with monolithic granite frames and ancient Thrumm bulk, carving cyclopean mountain halls and peak-fastnesses.
morgh.description: Massive, monolithic, and primal, the Morgh are rock-hewn stone ogre-like humanoids carrying ancient Thrumm blood closest to the surface. Standing 1.50m to 1.60m (4'11" to 5'3"), they are broad-shouldered, deep-chested, and immovable, built as cyclopean quarry-masons and subterranean hall-builders of Cragjaw Peaks. Their stone-skin grows in dense, rough cracked granite plates across shoulders, spine, and limbs. Their speech is slow and resonant, vibrating like grinding tectonic plates. They inhabit cyclopean stone halls and subterranean vat-fortresses carved deep into the mid-crag, gathering around common magma-kilns and forging megalithic stonework. A Morgh sentinel pulls a heavy ox-hide cowl over their craggy stone brow, leans on a staff, and does not move for days. The Morgh have been the Groven's bedrock craftsmen, hall-keepers, and forge-laborers since the Vat-Breakers' Revolt.
morgh.culturalBackground: The Morgh trace their lineage to the Groven who fled the vats but could not shed the old Thrumm instincts, the need to build, to guard, to bear weight in silence. Their hall-hearths are cyclopean subterranean halls carved deep into the Cragjaw Peaks, communal caverns heated by geothermal vents, shared among extended family around one great central fire. They speak the old earth tongue in the hall depths, reserving Common for dealings with Amordjin and outsiders. Their children learn stone-quarrying and bridge-tending before they learn bridge-tolling. Their elders die in the chasms, becoming the foundations of spans their grandchildren will walk.

traits.name: Stone-Scale Plating
traits.description: Your dense interlocking mineral plates grant +1 Durability (flat damage reduction against physical damage) and 15% physical damage resistance (permanent). You have 100% ember vulnerability.

effects.name: Stone-Scale Plating
effects.description: +1 Durability and 15% physical damage resistance from dense mineral plates.
effects.mechanicsText: Gain +1 Durability against physical damage and resist 15% of incoming physical damage from your dense mineral scale plating.

effects.name: Fire-Cracked Plates
effects.description: 100% ember vulnerability. Each ember hit: -5% physical resistance (max -15%). Recover plates after 1 hour resting on natural stone.
effects.mechanicsText: You are fully vulnerable to ember damage, and each ember hit cracks your plates, lowering physical resistance by 5% (up to 15%) until you rest on natural stone for an hour.

traits.name: Bridge-Warden's Wall
