The child is placed in a dark crypt-chamber with a sleeping parent and the soft glow of ancestors lining the walls, and taught to listen, to the drip of condensation, to the hum of the Root-Veil beneath the stone, to the names being sung two galleries above. The Mycellan do not teach their children to trust their eyes. They teach them to trust the dark, and to move through it without disturbing what the dark is holding.

The Tithing is the central ritual of Mycellan faith. Every month, each Mycellan household contributes a portion of their fungal harvest, a single cultivated cap, a vial of spore-dust, a length of mycelial thread, to the nearest Sunken Spire tithe-chamber. The tithe is not charity. It is maintenance: the dead in the crypts require fresh fungal shrouds to continue emitting light, and if the tithe ever stops, the crypts go dark. A family that misses its tithe is visited by a Veil-Speaker within three days, not to punish, but to ask if the family is still alive, because no living Mycellan would knowingly allow their ancestors' light to go out.

Spore-cultivation is the craft that sustains the monasteries. Every Mycellan, Bedel or Cromyx, learns to tend the fungal gardens that line the lower galleries: which strains produce food, which produce medicine, which produce light, which produce the volatile Ghost-Mycelium that must be handled with gloves of woven bog-cotton. The cultivators can read a bloom's health by the color of its glow, amber for healthy Deep-Glow, silver for stable Ghost-Mycelium, the sickly blue-white that means the strain is turning feral and must be burned before it spreads.

The Crypt-Vigil is the most sacred Mycellan practice and the one most dangerous to the Cromyx. A Veil-Speaker, or any Mycellan who wishes to undertake it, descends to the deepest crypt-chamber of a Sunken Spire and remains there for seven days without surfacing, maintaining the ancestral chant alone, communing with the Root-Veil and, through it, with wounded Morvane. The concentration of fungal light in the deepest chambers is intoxicating even to the Bedel. To the Cromyx, it is almost unbearable, and almost irresistible. A Cromyx who completes a Crypt-Vigil without over-lighting is considered to have proven something about their bloodline that no one can take from them. A Cromyx who over-lights during a Vigil is added to the Inquisition's ledger and to the chant-rotation, their name sung as a warning forever.

Death rites are simple and grueling. The dying Mycellan is carried to the nearest Sunken Spire and laid in the crypt-chamber that corresponds to their bloodline and generation. The Veil-Speakers wrap the body in a living fungal shroud, a sheet of cultivated Deep-Glow or Ghost-Mycelium, depending on the deceased's bloodline, and begin singing their name into the rotation. The body is not buried. It is not burned. It is left on the crypt-shelf, wrapped in its shroud, and the family trusts that the fungal bond will produce light for as long as the deceased's bloodline remembers them. A Mycellan whose name is no longer sung goes dark. A Mycellan whose name is sung every rotation for a thousand years continues to emit a faint, steady glow, the same color as their eyes in life, and just as difficult to look away from.

birthrightQuestions.description: At character creation, choose which echo of the wounded Root-Veil you carry, the moment Morvane's curse touched you most deeply, the dimming or brightening that recurs in your dreams and surfaces in the presence of certain spores, names, or silences.

prompts.name: The Parent
prompts.question: You held your parent's hand as their lantern-light dimmed. The fungal shroud had already been woven; the Veil-Speakers were already singing the first rotation of their name. But in the last hour, your parent's rust-amber eyes went dark for the first time in two centuries, and the crypt around you dimmed with them. You have the exact shade of their final dimming memorized. It surfaces in your second pulse during moments of stress, and when you close your eyes in a quiet crypt, you can still feel the warmth leaving their hand. Choose: what were their last words to you? Once per long rest, when you fail a saving throw against fear, you may hear their voice beneath the panic and reroll the save, but you take 1d4 wyrd damage as the echo of their dimming replays fresh.

prompts.name: The Patient
prompts.question: Your first failure as a spore-healer. The corruption had spread too deep. You arrived too late, or the Ghost-Mycelium had already reached the heart, or the wound was too deep for even fungal-thread to close. You felt them slip, not fear but surprise, as if they had not expected to die in front of someone who was supposed to save them. You still know their name. You still visit their crypt during the annual Remembrance, and you still apologize to a glow that cannot hear you. Choose: what was their name, and what were they to you, a stranger, a neighbor, a friend? You have advantage on Medicine checks made to stabilize dying creatures. But when you fail to save someone, the GM may ask you: does this remind you of them?
prompts.buffOnStabilize: advantage on Medicine checks to stabilize dying creatures
prompts.narrativeCost: GM may invoke the memory on a failed save

prompts.name: The Innocent
prompts.question: As a crypt-acolyte, you tended a rite that went wrong. A spore-blessing meant to strengthen a failing initiate instead accelerated their transformation, the Ghost-Mycelium flared, their features twisted further toward the feral, and they fled the monastery into the deep caves. The Veil-Speakers recorded it as the initiate's own instability. You knew the truth: you had misread the bloom, used a feral strain when you meant to use a stable one. No one else knows. You did not speak up, because to admit the error would have ended your vocation and cast shame on your bloodline. The initiate lives still, somewhere in the deep, more changed than they should be. Choose: why didn't you speak? You have advantage on Insight checks made to detect deception. But whenever you give testimony or make a judgment, the GM may ask: are you sure?
prompts.buffOnInsight: advantage on Insight checks to detect deception
prompts.narrativeCost: GM may call your certainty into question when you testify

prompts.name: The Over-Lit Kin
prompts.question: You are, or were, an Inquisitor. You killed your own blood: a cousin, a sibling, a friend who over-lit past the point of recovery. You tracked them through the deep caves by spore-sign and the sound of their burning glow, you found them in the dead-end dark, and you ended them. Their final breath was not fear. It was not pain. It was relief, the hush had been screaming in their skull for years, and your blade was the first silence they had felt since the addiction took hold. You don't know what to do with that. Choose: who were they to you? When you deal damage to a Cromyx enemy, you deal +1d4 wyrd damage, you know exactly where the hush has weakened them, because you have studied the addiction your whole life. But you cannot harm a Cromyx who has surrendered without reliving the moment, and you suffer 1d4 wyrd damage each time you do.
prompts.costOnSurrender: 1d4 wyrd damage when harming a surrendered Cromyx

clean.name: Bedel
clean.illustrationCaption: “Beneath the peat and root-canopy, the Bedel keep vigil where sunlight cannot burn.” — Veil-Speaker Tradition

illustrations.caption: “Beneath the peat and root-canopy, the Bedel keep vigil where sunlight cannot burn.” — Veil-Speaker Tradition
“To unmask in the crypt is to greet the ancestors without pretense or vanity.” — Rites of the Deep Cloister
“Carved into the inverted stalactite vaults, the Sunken Spire hangs above the abyssal mire — an eternal testament to faith in the deep.” — Architecture of the Veiled
“The book does not end with burial; every page turned is a life recalled to service.” — Matriarch Isara Deep-Glow
“No trespasser crosses the gatehouse threshold until the toll of silence has been paid.” — Inquisitor Orven the Still-Handed

clean.visualDescription: The inheritors of Deep-Glow, the oldest and most stable fungal strain, the Bedel bear their transformation lightly. Their features are closer to the original elven forms than any other Mycellan, elegant cheekbones, long tapered limbs, ears that curl only gently, and their lantern-eyes burn a controlled rust-amber, warm and steady, easily dimmed in polite company. They favor dark monastic cassocks embroidered with fungal-thread that marks bloodline and vocation. Pale-skinned and composed, they move with the quiet authority of people whose biology has never been a war, and they are accustomed to being stared at but never to being doubted.
clean.tooltipSummary: Steadfast crypt-keepers whose stable Deep-Glow blood leaves them closer to the old elven forms, moving through the world with composed rust-amber sight and quiet authority.
clean.description: The inheritors of Deep-Glow, the oldest and most stable fungal strain, bonded to their ancestors in the deep caves before the Wyrd wounded Morvane. Their transformation was less severe: their features are closer to their original elven forms, their lantern-eyes burn a controlled rust-amber, warm and steady, easily dimmed in polite company. The Deep-Glow strain threads less deeply through their nervous systems, leaves their minds more stable, their bodies more composed. They are near-total immune to the Over-Lit addiction: not morally superior, merely less entangled in Morvane's wound, carrying a strain that does not intoxicate. Disproportionately represented in trade delegations, crypt-councils, scriptorium gatekeeping, and every position that faces the outside world. Their privilege is invisible to them, they have never had to fight the hush, so they do not understand why the Cromyx cannot simply resist it. The flaw they carry is the quiet assumption that their biological luck is a form of virtue.
clean.culturalBackground:
The Bedel trace their bloodline to the first Mycellan who carried Deep-Glow, the stable, warm-amber fungal strain that threads least deeply through the nervous system and produces steady light with minimal intoxication. Their tradition is continuity: the scriptoriums, the crypt-councils, the trade routes, the diplomatic missions to Athien grave-cities and Solari forge-halls. The Bedel are the face the Mycellan show to outsiders, and they have been the face for so long that they have begun to forget there are other Mycellan in the dark who look nothing like them.

Bedel children are educated in the scriptoriums from the age when their lantern-eyes first steady, around six or seven. They learn to read fungal-wood records, to recite crypt-genealogies, to tend the spore-gardens and cultivate the strains that sustain the monastery. By adolescence they are expected to choose a vocation: Veil-Speaker (priesthood), Inscriptor (record-keeper), Witch Doctor (spore-healer), or Inquisitor (hunter). The last is the least common among the Bedel, their senses are less acute than the Cromyx's, and hunting an Over-Lit through the deep caves with dimmer eyes is a test few Bedel volunteer for.

They view the Cromyx with a complex, carefully unspoken mixture of pity and fear. The Cromyx are their siblings, their cousins, their children who inherited a different strain. The Bedel recognize the Cromyx's sharper perception of the Root-Veil. They rely on it, the best cultivators and readers of the underground in Mycellan society are overwhelmingly Cromyx. But the Bedel also control the institutions that record, govern, and trade, and none of those institutions have a Cromyx majority. The Bedel call this "stability." The Cromyx call it what it is.

The Bedel rarely leave the Bryngloom Forest. When they do, they travel in monastic vestments, dark cassocks with fungal-thread embroidery marking their bloodline and vocation, and their rust-amber eyes draw stares in human settlements, Athien trade-hubs, and Solari forge-halls alike. The Bedel are accustomed to being stared at. They are not accustomed to being doubted.

traits.name: Deep-Glow Blood
traits.description: Immune to the Over-Lit (Hush) addiction and resistant to blight damage; darkvision limited to 30 feet; disadvantage on Intimidation checks against non-Mycellan. The Deep-Glow strain that protects you is warm, steady, and mercifully dim, a crypt-keeper's light rather than a predator's, though it also leaves your perception of the Root-Veil fainter than the Cromyx's.

effects.name: Hush-Immunity
effects.description: Immune to the Over-Lit addiction and resistant to blight damage. Your Deep-Glow blood is stable, ancient, and cannot be intoxicated by the fungal strains that consume the Cromyx.

statusEffect.description: Immune to Over-Lit addiction. Resistant to blight damage.

effects.mechanicsText: Immune to the Over-Lit (hush) addiction and resistant to blight damage from the stable Deep-Glow bloodline.

effects.name: The Dim Root
effects.description: Your darkvision is limited to 30 feet. Your perception of the Root-Veil is fainter than the Cromyx's, you sense less of the mycelial network's pulse, and what you do sense arrives slower and dimmer.
effects.mechanicsText: Darkvision capped at 30 feet; fainter, slower perception of the Root-Veil than the Cromyx.

effects.name: Warm Eyes
effects.description: Disadvantage on Intimidation checks against non-Mycellan. Your rust-amber eyes are warm, steady, and unmistakably gentle, a crypt-keeper's light, not a predator's.
effects.mechanicsText: Disadvantage on Intimidation checks against non-Mycellan targets due to warm, gentle lantern-eyes.

traits.name: Crypt-Record
traits.description: +2 to History and Medicine checks involving Bryngloom Forest, the Athien, fungal substrate, crypt-genealogies, or death-lore; this bonus is lost if you go 24 hours without spending at least 1 hour maintaining your personal crypt-record, and is recovered only by catching up. You were trained in the scriptoriums (the only formal education the Mycellan offer) and can read fungal-wood tablets and recite the dead as fluently as any Veil-Speaker, though the records do not maintain themselves and the backlog does not forgive.

effects.name: Scriptorium-Trained
effects.description: +2 to History and Medicine checks related to Bryngloom Forest, the Athien, fungal substrate, crypt-genealogies, or death-related lore. You have spent years reading what the dead left written.
effects.mechanicsText: +2 to History and Medicine checks involving Bryngloom Forest, the Athien, fungal substrate, crypt-genealogies, or death-lore; lost without daily record maintenance.

effects.name: The Unwritten Debt
effects.description: You must spend 1 hour per long rest maintaining your personal crypt-record, reciting names, updating genealogies, recording new deaths you have witnessed. If you miss this maintenance, lose the Crypt-Record bonus until you spend 1 hour catching up. The backlog accumulates: two missed days = the bonus remains lost for 2 hours after you resume. Three missed days = you must spend a full long rest catching up before the bonus returns.

statusEffect.description: Lose Crypt-Record bonus after 24 hours without maintenance. Recover by spending 1+ hours reciting records.

effects.mechanicsText: Lose the Crypt-Record bonus after 24 hours without 1 hour of maintenance; recover by catching up, with backlog scaling.

traits.name: Veil-Speaker's Chant
traits.description: Bedel bloodlines have sung the names of the dead since the first Sunken Spire was carved into the bog, a genealogy in melody, a rotation of remembrance that has not broken in seventeen centuries. You have learned the ancestral chants of your bloodline's crypt: the names, the order, the rise and fall of a song older than any written record in the Gloom. Once per short rest, you may spend 1 minute singing the names of your ancestors to grant one ally within 30 feet advantage on their next saving throw before the end of your next long rest. The chant requires your full voice, and it announces you, all creatures within 120 feet who can hear know your exact location, and your lantern-eyes brighten involuntarily for the duration. An ancestor whose name is never sung goes dark. You have promised not to be the one who stops.

effects.name: Ancestral Blessing
effects.description: One ally within 30ft gains advantage on their next saving throw before end of your next long rest.
effects.mechanicsText: One ally within 30 ft gains advantage on their next saving throw before the end of your next long rest.

effects.name: Lantern-Bloom
effects.description: Your lantern-eyes brighten for the chant duration, all within 120ft know your location.

statusEffect.description: Announced location within 120ft during chanting.

effects.mechanicsText: All creatures within 120 ft learn your exact location while you chant, and your lantern-eyes brighten involuntarily.

traits.name: Crypt-Pulse
traits.description: Once per long rest, channel ancestral fungal-light through your hands to heal a creature you touch for 1d8+Spirit HP. The crypt-light that sustains the dead can also sustain the living.

effects.name: Crypt-Light Healing
effects.description: Heal a creature you touch for 1d8+Spirit HP. The ancestral fungal-light courses through your hands into the living.

marked.name: Cromyx
marked.illustrationCaption: “The root-paths twist through black mud; the sickle reaps only what the swamp allows.” — Cromyx Stalker Maxim

illustrations.caption: “The root-paths twist through black mud; the sickle reaps only what the swamp allows.” — Cromyx Stalker Maxim
“Mirehollow rises upon the buttress roots, swaying with the marsh tides yet never yielding to the flood.” — Stilt-Haven Annals
“Harvest in the dead of twilight, when the bioluminescent spores glow brightest and the water is still.” — Blight-Harvester Garrow

marked.visualDescription: The inheritors of Ghost-Mycelium, Morvane's wounded nerve-tissue made symbiotic. The Cromyx share the compact wiry frame and vestigial elven architecture of their kin, but their lantern-eyes burn silver-white and will not dim easily, flaring with anger, flickering with grief, brightening under any strong emotion so that their hearts are readable across a room. Their ear-tips curl more sharply. The volatile strain threads deeper through them: their presence is impossible to hide in darkness, and the brilliant light that makes their perception extraordinary is the same light that consumes them from within.
marked.tooltipSummary: Ghost-sighted beacon-carriers whose branded eyes blaze with Morvane's wounded nerve-tissue, perceiving the Root-Veil most keenly even as the Hush tempts them with every step.
marked.description: The inheritors of Ghost-Mycelium, Morvane's wounded nerve-tissue made symbiotic, the volatile, brilliant, painful strain that amplifies perception and sensitivity at the cost of stability. Their lantern-eyes burn silver-white and do not dim easily; their emotions are readable from across a room, their presence impossible to hide in darkness. Their perception of the Root-Veil is extraordinary: they sense the mycelial network's pulse more clearly than any Bedel, read the spore-signatures of the underground, detect things other Mycellan cannot. They are also the most vulnerable to the Over-Lit addiction, their sensitivity is both gift and curse, and every Cromyx family carries at least one Over-Lit relative. Stigmatized by the Bedel as unreliable, dangerous, the bloodline most deeply entangled in the wounded god. The flaw they carry is their own biology: the light that makes them extraordinary is the same light that consumes them from within.
marked.culturalBackground:
The Cromyx trace their bloodline to the Mycellan most deeply touched by Morvane's wound, those who carry Ghost-Mycelium, the brilliant, silver-white fungal strain that is the deity's injured nerve-tissue made symbiotic. Their tradition is sensitivity: the Root-Veil read at acute depth, the spore-signatures of the underground sensed where the Bedel perceive only faint hum, the Over-Lit kin tracked into the deep caves by the same bond that will one day betray the tracker.

Cromyx children learn to feel the Root-Veil before they learn to speak, their Ghost-Mycelium bond is active from birth, silver-white pinpoints flickering in the cradle. By the time a Cromyx child can walk, they are already attuned to the mycelial network's pulse: they sense the health of the fungal gardens, the shift in the bog's currents, the distant tremor of something moving through the deep caves. They are taught to dim their eyes, a skill the Bedel never need to practice, and most never fully master it. A Cromyx's lantern-eyes flicker with their emotions, flare with their anger, dim with their grief. They are the most honest people in the Bryngloom Forest, and the most exposed.

Every Cromyx family has at least one Over-Lit relative. The numbers are not a matter of debate, they are recorded in the scriptoriums, which are maintained by the Bedel. The Cromyx believe the Bedel underreport the epidemic to minimize its political impact. The Bedel believe the Cromyx exaggerate their suffering to gain exploit in crypt-council negotiations. Neither side has proof. Both sides have centuries of resentment.

The Cromyx are disproportionately represented among the Inquisitors, the order that hunts Over-Lit Mycellan who have progressed past recovery. This is not because the Bedel forbid Bedel from joining. It is because the Bedel's fainter Root-Veil sense makes them less effective trackers, and because the psychological burden of killing your own kind falls more heavily on a Bedel who has never felt the hush's pull than on a Cromyx who has spent their entire life fighting it. The Cromyx who join the Inquisition are the most respected and most isolated Mycellan in the Gloom, feared by the Over-Lit they hunt, pitied by the Bedel who no longer sit beside them at crypt-feasts, and quietly, desperately envied by the Cromyx who have not yet fallen.

The Cromyx rarely serve as trade delegates or diplomatic envoys. Their eyes are too bright, they unsettle human merchants, make Athien negotiators uncomfortable, and remind the Solari of something their Sun-Speakers have been prophesying for centuries but will not name. When a Cromyx leaves the Bryngloom Forest, it is because they have chosen to, and the choice marks them as someone who has accepted that the outside world will stare and flinch and reach for iron that does not burn them but still, somehow, hurts to look at.

traits.name: Ghost-Mycelium Sight
traits.description: Darkvision 90 feet; advantage on Perception checks to track creatures or detect hidden objects, passages, and traps; automatically sense any creature within 60 feet that drops below 25% of its maximum HP; but disadvantage on Stealth in all lighting, your eyes glow visibly from 120 feet in darkness, and creatures have advantage on Perception to detect you in dim light or darkness. Your silver-white Ghost-Mycelium eyes burn with Morvane's wounded nerve-tissue, a beacon that reads the Root-Veil's pulse for miles even as it reveals you in turn.

effects.name: The Long Root
effects.description: Darkvision 90 feet. Advantage on Perception checks made to track creatures or detect hidden objects, passages, and traps, your Ghost-Mycelium bond reads the Root-Veil's pulse and senses what the underground has tried to hide.
effects.mechanicsText: Darkvision 90 ft; advantage on Perception checks to track creatures or detect hidden objects, passages, and traps.

effects.name: Death-Sense
effects.description: You automatically detect any creature within 60 feet that is below 25% of its maximum HP. The failing root-connections forming around them are visible to you as a distinct, cold silver halo, unmistakable, involuntary, and growing.

effects.name: The Unhidden Light
effects.description: Disadvantage on Stealth checks in any lighting condition. Your silver-white lantern-eyes are visible in darkness from 120 feet away, a beacon that cannot be hooded, cloaked, or extinguished. Creatures have advantage on Perception checks to detect you in dim light or darkness.
effects.mechanicsText: Disadvantage on Stealth checks in all lighting; eyes visible from 120 ft in darkness; enemies have advantage to detect you in dim light or darkness.

traits.name: The Hush-Temptation
traits.description: Your Ghost-Mycelium bond is a double-edged gift. You can amplify your perception of the Root-Veil to extraordinary levels, tasting every spore-signature within miles, reading the mycelial network's deep currents, perceiving the wounded land's pulse in ways no Bedel bond could ever reach. But the hush sings in your blood, and every amplification brings you closer to the light that does not let go.

effects.name: The Brightening
effects.description: For 10 minutes, your Root-Veil perception reaches its maximum potential: advantage on Perception, Insight, and Investigation checks. Your lantern-eyes blaze silver-white, visible from 300 feet in darkness, and the mycelial network's deep currents open to you like a book written in a language you were born to read.
effects.mechanicsText: For 10 minutes while amplified: advantage on Perception, Insight, and Investigation checks; lantern-eyes blaze silver-white, visible from 300 ft.

effects.name: The Hush's Pull
effects.description: When the Brightening ends, make a DC 14 Spirit saving throw. On a failure, the Over-Lit's hunger surfaces: you suffer -2 to all d20 rolls until you complete a short rest, as the hush screams in the back of your skull and every fungal light you pass whispers your name. On a success, you resist, the pull was there, but it was not strong enough. This time.

statusEffect.description: DC 14 Spirit save after Brightening. On failure: -2 to all d20 rolls until short rest.

effects.mechanicsText: When the Brightening ends, make a DC 14 Spirit saving throw; on failure, suffer -2 to all d20 rolls until the next short rest.

traits.name: Root-Veil Echo
traits.description: The Ghost-Mycelium bond that gives you acute Root-Veil perception does not merely read the present, it echoes the recent past like a stone dropped in still water, the ripples visible long after the impact has vanished. Once per long rest, you may touch a surface in a location where events occurred within the last hour and experience an echo: you learn what creatures were present, their emotional states, and a shadow of their intent, enough to know whether they meant harm, whether they were fleeing, whether they were searching. The echo does not reveal faces or exact words, only the shape of what happened, written in the Root-Veil's own memory. But every echo pulls at the root, you gain 1 level of Exhaustion after using this ability, a cost paid not by the body but by the fungal bond itself, which must regrow the tendril you burned to reach backward through the mycelial network.

selectedEffects.name: Root-Veil Echo
selectedEffects.description: 1/long rest: touch surface to sense creatures present in last hour, their emotional states, and shadow of intent. No faces or words.

effects.name: Echo Insight
effects.description: Learn presence, emotional state, and intent-shadow of creatures who were at this location within 1 hour.

effects.name: Root-Burn
effects.description: Gain 1 level of Exhaustion after using Root-Veil Echo, the fungal bond must regrow the tendril burned by reaching backward.

statusEffect.description: 1 level of Exhaustion after use.

effects.mechanicsText: Gain 1 level of Exhaustion after using Root-Veil Echo as the burned fungal tendril regrows.

traits.name: Death-Mark Strike
traits.description: Once per short rest, mark a target within 30 feet with your Ghost-Mycelium bond. For 1 minute, you know their exact location even through walls, and your attacks against them deal +1d4 blight damage. The Ghost-Mycelium does not forget what it has touched.

effects.name: Death-Cromyx
effects.description: For 1 minute, you know the target's exact location even through walls, and your attacks against them deal +1d4 blight damage.

effects.name: Cromyx for Death
effects.description: The target is marked by Ghost-Mycelium sight: their location is known to the Cromyx, and attacks against them deal +1d4 blight damage.

statusEffect.description: Location always known to the marker. +1d4 blight damage from their attacks.

effects.mechanicsText: Cromyx target location is always known to the marker, even through walls; marker attacks deal +1d4 blight damage for 1 minute.

solari.name: Solari
solari.essence: Devoted cave-dwelling nomads, keepers of Sol's last ember
solari.illustrationCaption: “Deep within Caldera-Hollow, the heartbeat of the sleeping child warms our stone long after the surface sun has failed.” — Chronicler of the Deep Hearth
solari.cardFlavor: Ash-dusted forge-clans descended from human Solvarn, tending Sol's Breath while the conscious, unhatched child remains protected below.
solari.visualDescription: Broad-shouldered and solid, standing 5'10" to 6'4" and weighing 190 to 280 pounds. Their skin is a warm, earthy dark brown-beige with a fine grey dusting of mineral-ash that sheds when they move or under stress. Their eyes are enormous and solid black, absorbing light rather than reflecting it — on the surface, they wear thick ash-tinted eye-cloths to filter the painful daylight. Their forearms and shoulders bear deliberate burn-scars and forge-marks encoding clan affiliation, trade, and lineage in a visual language. They wear their hair in dreadlocks. Their bearing is deliberately calm and still, the discipline of the Vault-Breath made visible in every unhurried movement.
solari.description:
**[The Cinder-Born Clans]**, *Deep in the dark vaults of Sundale, a broad, still figure sits in absolute contemplation, dark brown-beige skin lit by the faint glow of the Sol's Breath, holding a moment of perfect silence before the last ember of Sol.*

Broad-shouldered and solid, the Solari are a people shaped by the deep. Their skin is a warm, earthy dark brown-beige, the tone of a people who have lived in volcanic landscapes for generations, running grey with a fine dusting of dry mineral-ash that sheds when they move or suffer stress. They are strong, not brutish or hulking, but solidly built from a life of navigating caves, climbing volcanic rock, and enduring the physical demands of subterranean existence. Their eyes are enormous and solid black, absorbing light rather than reflecting it, adapted to perceive the faintest heat-gradient in the absolute darkness of the subterranean vaults where they sheltered after Sol went dark. On the surface, they wear thick, ash-tinted eye-cloths to filter the daylight that pains those dark-adapted eyes.

The Solari descend from human Solvarn antecedents altered through celestial infusion. Their brown-beige flesh, mineral-ash dusting, black eyes and heat-adapted lungs are ordinary ancestry, not basalt bodies or lava fissures. They do not need external forge-flame to survive. Sol is alive, conscious and unhatched in the core; Sol's Breath is a thermal connection interpreted by tending-clans, not his last surviving consciousness. Forge-marks encode lineage and craft, while devotion is a cultural choice.
solari.overview:
When Sol spoke to the Solari, it was never in words. The Sun-Speakers, the eldest cinder-keepers, crouched in the geothermal vents at dawn and received pulses of thermal radiation and fading heat-signatures that guided their great descent. They dug not to hide, but to survive, excavating the thermal deep beneath Sundale because they knew the open winter skies would be harsh and unforgiving.

Human Solvarn miners and vent-readers worked the thermal deep before the Star-Fall. Celestial infusion later produced Solari lineages. Solar concealment began the Long Cold, not Sol's death or sleep. Sun-Speakers interpret heat and impressions from Sol's Breath; accounts of one final image belong to their liturgy, not a guarantee that every clan received a spoken or infallible command.

They emerged when Emberspire erupted, reclaiming the volcanic ashlands because the surface had warmed enough to range across comfortably. They rebuilt their forge-clans around active calderas, resumed the old ways: sun-prayers at dawn, the Sol's Breath tended by an order of Sun-Speakers who listen every morning to a silence that grows colder every year. The Solari are religious fanatics, but grounded, practical fanatics. They tend the forge not because they will die without it, but because the forge is the altar of their faith, and the Sol's Breath is the most important thing in the world. They organize their entire civilization around keeping it burning.
quickFacts: Forge-clans of Sundale, descended from human Solvarn altered through celestial infusion. Human antecedents worked the vents before the Binding; Sol remains conscious and unhatched.

Dark brown-beige skin dusted with volcanic ash, glowing scar-traced forge-marks that encode clan, trade, and lineage. Their lungs filter ash, their dark-adapted eyes see heat, and they wear ash-tinted eye-cloths on the surface.
Play a Solari to protect warmth, practice craft, or question the institutions that price devotion. Korr keep deep-vault traditions; Anhur range the ashlands.
solari.culturalBackground:
Solari society is organized into forge-clans bound to volcanic calderas. These clans are bloodlines, each with its own ancestral forge and practice of the Vault-Breath. Clan identity is worn visibly: every Solari's forearms and shoulders are marked at birth with deliberate burn-scars, a process called the Marking-Rite. The scars encode clan, trade, and lineage in a visual language. The marks darken with proximity to the Sol's Breath; Vault-Keeper marks are stark and crisp, while Ash-Ranger marks are fainter and blurred at the edges.

Settlements are built around the forges as altars. The forge is where the Sol's Breath is kept by the clan currently entrusted with its tending. Sol's silence taught the Solari patience, and patience is the highest virtue.

The surface ashlands are barely hospitable to anyone else, but the Solari breathe them comfortably. Their lungs developed thick mucosal membranes that filter ash. The cost: in clean, humid climates, their lungs grow sluggish.

Their society is a meritocracy of craft and endurance. The greatest terror in Solari culture is the slow, permanent cooling of the Sol's Breath. The clan that currently holds the Sol's Breath has been lying about its health, and the other clans are beginning to splinter.
solari.variantDiversity: The Solari are divided into two subraces: Vault-Keeper Solari (Korr lineage), deep-vault forge-masters who stay near the Sol's Breath core and train their bodies for absolute stillness; and Ash-Ranger Solari (Anhur lineage), surface scouts who venture onto the frozen borders in heavy insulating wraps and range the volcanic wastes.

integrationNotes.actionPointSystem: Solari abilities focus on endurance, forge-craft, and patient combat. Their underground ancestry grants them stillness, ash-resistance, and dark-adapted senses, not fire magic, but the hard-earned adaptations of a people who survived the deep.
integrationNotes.backgroundSynergy: Solari excel in backgrounds emphasizing crafting, endurance, and spiritual devotion. Their sun-reverent culture and clan-mark identity complement paths of tradition, craft, and unyielding patience.
integrationNotes.classCompatibility: The Korr are the deep-vault people, and their native paths are the Spellguard (absorb geothermal instability into a disciplined body), the Martyr (the Vault-Witness, still and absorbing), the Pyrofiend (the Banked Hearth, control through stillness), and the Augur (reading the Sol's Breath's dimming). The Anhur are the surface forge-clans: native to the Crusader (they smelted the dead god's shards into their own plate), the Martyr (the Ash-Witness, stepping into the burning debris), the Pyrofiend (forge conversion, more basalt than flesh), and the Spellguard (angling the blast away from kin). No other people owns these paths.

solari.diasporaVariation: Solari diaspora clusters wherever geothermal heat is available. The Harath-Vault Korr are the deep-vault archetype, but Cragjaw-diaspora Solari (around the Steam-Line Cartel's geothermal pipes at Frostmaw) run hotter and more active, their burn-scars blurred by the different mineral profile of Cragjaw water. The Bloodhammer-Sump Solari of Nordhalla, a small community around the geothermal skirmish-grounds, have intermarried enough with Skald to develop a cold-tolerance their southern kin lack, though they still keep daily vigil at whatever forge they can find. Sundale is the only region with a large Solari population; elsewhere they are rare, devoted expatriates who carry their faith to whatever geothermal outpost will have them.
solari.meaningfulTradeoffs: Solari possess formidable physical endurance and ash-resistance but suffer fatigue in clean, humid air and are deeply vulnerable to the cold, not because they are metabolically dependent on fire, but because their bodies are adapted to volcanic environments and struggle in damp, clean climates. Their dark-adapted black eyes struggle in daylight. Their deliberate stillness is a cultural and devotional strength, and a social liability among faster, more fidget-prone races.
solari.epicHistory:
Human Solvarn antecedents excavated Sundale's thermal deep in the Long Before. Their vent-reading and engineering preceded celestial infusion, which produced the Solari at the Binding. Later Sun-Speakers interpret thermal impressions through trained practice and doctrine; they did not receive universal instructions from an asleep or dying Sol.

Aex protected her conscious, unhatched son in the core while Aethil maintained the sky-ward. The Long Cold followed concealment of solar radiance. Sol's Breath carries warmth through geological networks; some tending traditions describe a cupped ember as their founding vision. The child remains awake, and an institution's interpretation does not establish his consent or intentions.

The centuries underground were not a hibernation. They were a civilization. The Solari built forge-clans in the dark, bloodlines organized around ancestral forges, each clan tracing its origin to one of the original Sun-Speakers. They developed the forge-mark system, encoding clan identity, trade, and ancestor-lineage into deliberate burn-scar patterns on the forearms. They learned stillness, not as meditation, but as survival: in cramped tunnels where oxygen was scarce, children who could not sit motionless for hours simply did not survive to adulthood. They call this discipline the Vault-Breath, and it has become the foundation of Solari spirituality.

When the Blind Strike fractured Aex's continental ward — Keth Amar crashing into the planetary seal the Secret Aegis alone held — the volcanic pressure that erupted across the world reached Sundale first. Emberspire exploded. Predatory Wyrd, seeded for twenty-five years through the Whispered Purge, bled from every new crack. And the Solari, already beneath the eruption, already adapted to ash and heat and the long, grinding patience of the deep, emerged onto a surface they had not walked in generations. They reclaimed their ancestral ashlands. They rebuilt their forge-clans around the geothermal vents. They resumed the sun-prayers at dawn, the Vigil of the Sol's Breath, the old ways that had sustained them through centuries of darkness.

The Wars of Molten Earth came later, when surface kingdoms, desperate for volcanic resources, attempted to seize Solari forge-clans by force. The Solari fought not as a unified army but as two bloodlines with distinct ways of war. The clans held. The invaders burned. The Forge Accords were established in the aftermath: Solari would never war against Solari. All forges would serve all clans. The Sol's Breath would be held by a single tending-clan, rotated by covenant, never hoarded. The Accords have held for generations.

Now the Sol's Breath is dimming. The tending-clan has known for three generations and concealed it, executing shamans who spoke the truth, fabricating reports of stable brightness, maintaining their power by managing a lie that grows heavier every year. The Korr tending-clan began concealing the Sol's Breath's measurable dimming after the False Dawn Riots, two decades into the Freezing Era. The concealment lasted three generations, passed from matriarch to matriarch, until the Sol's Breath could no longer be hidden. The other clans are beginning to splinter. Some demand transparency. Some accuse the tenders of causing the dimming through mismanagement. Some whisper that the dimming is Keth Amar's slow victory, the last ember of Sol being consumed from within, like the spirit it came from. And some, the youngest and most reckless, whisper that the Sol's Breath was never Sol's gift at all, that it is Keth Amar's tether, a feeding-line the predator left behind when it breached the seal, and that the Solari have spent centuries tending the wrong fire.

The tending-clans dispute what the dimming means: failing channels, hostile pressure, or a duty misunderstood. Sol is already conscious; a vent's decline does not automatically mean hatching, death, or Keth's guaranteed victory. The End-Vigil is a campaign crisis with defined triggers, not a universal countdown imposed on every new game.

notableFigures.name: Thaeron
notableFigures.title: Keeper of the Freezing Era Flame
notableFigures.backstory:
The eldest living Sun-Speaker, Thaeron has tended the Sol's Breath for sixty years. His skin is weathered dark brown-beige, cross-hatched with age-lines that trace the pattern of old lava-flows across his forearms. His eyes, enormous even for a Solari, the pupils barely distinguishable from the solid black sclera, have stared into the Sol's Breath's light for so long that he claims to see colors in it that younger shamans cannot perceive. He does not speak of what those colors mean.

Thaeron belongs to the tending-clan, the bloodline currently entrusted with the Sol's Breath. He is the only living Solari who has known for certain that the ember is dimming for more than fifty years. He has never told anyone. Not his apprentices. Not his clan-elders. Not the other forge-clans who demand transparency. His silence has preserved the Forge Accords through three generations of slow, incremental cooling. He believes, with the unshakeable certainty of a man who has spent six decades staring into dying fire, that revealing the truth would shatter Solari civilization more completely than the dimming itself.

Thaeron does not believe the Sol's Breath is Keth Amar's tether. But he also does not believe it is Sol's gift. He has a third theory, one he has never spoken aloud, one he barely allows himself to think, that the Sol's Breath is neither spirit nor predator but a test, and that the Solari were never meant to tend it forever. They were meant to let it go. He cannot bring himself to test this theory, because testing it might mean watching the last ember of Sol die in his hands.

notableFigures.name: Vaelith
notableFigures.title: The Ash-Shrouded
notableFigures.backstory:
The most traveled living messenger of the forge-clans, Vaelith has crossed every volcanic wasteland in Sundale five times, on foot, alone, carrying nothing but a sealed message-tube and the marks of her clan. Her skin is lighter than most Solari from decades of constant ash-wind exposure, the grain worn smooth across her shoulders where the storms hit hardest. Her eye-wraps are so permanently stained with volcanic ash that they have become part of her face; no living Solari has seen her without them.

Vaelith is the only messenger trusted by all three forge-clan bloodlines. During the escalating tensions over the Sol's Breath's health, she has carried sealed accusations, denials, threats, and pleas between the clans, always sealed, always private, never read. The tending-clan trusts her because she has never broken a seal. The doubting-clans trust her because she has never been seen favoring the tenders. The truth is more complicated: Vaelith has been reading the seals anyway. Not the messages, the seals. She can tell by the way a clan presses its sigil into the cooling wax whether the hand that pressed it was trembling.

She keeps a private record, pressed ash-tablets, hidden in a fissure beneath the Sol's Breath's chamber, of every tremor she has felt, dated, catalogued. The tending-clan's hands have been trembling for eleven years.

majorLocations.name: The Harath-Vault
majorLocations.description:
Carved radially into the volcanic throat of a dormant secondary caldera three miles from Emberspire sits the massive subterranean capital of the Solari forge-clans. Carved out by the Sun-Speakers centuries before the sun's death, the Vault is a titanic, sprawling underground city of craftsmen, miners, and priests. Grated catwalks are suspended above hot, molten metal rivers that rush through the center of the pathways, acting as both the source of the city's immense heat and its primary defensive barrier. The sounds of hammers falling rings out through the hustle and bustle of the stone avenues.

At the Vault's absolute center is **The Great Forge**, where oversized obsidian anvils are worked diligently by craftsmen who barely break a sweat under the unbearable heat. In the inner ring sits **The Harath-Chamber**, a massive monastic sanctuary of pure basalt where the **Korr Sun-Speakers** kneel in six-hour shifts, practicing the Vault-Breath in absolute silence around the **Sol's Breath**, the stone bowl containing the last eternal ember of Sol. The outer rings contain the residential sectors and the alchemical laboratories of the **Fex**, who trade alchemical reagents and gear-work for Solari obsidian.

majorLocations.name: The Shyr
majorLocations.description: A ninety-mile scar of cooling basalt, the Shyr serves as the Solari's primary thoroughfare, a road of stone that walks itself as the lava cools and contracts into predictable fracture-patterns. The Shyr is not a wasteland. It is the Solari's main artery of survival, where Anhur surface badland-hunters and miners build temporary volcanic outposts, constantly navigating shifting thermal vents and guarding the basalt trade roads from ice-pirates and freezing border beasts.

solari.currentCrisis:
The Sol's Breath is dying, a truth the tending-clan (Korr) has concealed for three generations. The dimming has accelerated in the last decade, and the Sun-Speakers who attempted to speak openly were silenced. Those who remain have split into three camps:

The Risen hold to the old faith: Sol is sleeping, the ember is merely resting, and patience will be rewarded when the spirit rekindles and speaks again. They advocate for continued silence, continued waiting, continued devotion, the same path the Korr have walked for centuries. They control the tending-clan's official position.

The Sunderer, a smaller, heretical faction, believe the Sol's Breath was never Sol's gift at all. They argue that the ember is Keth Amar's tether, a feeding-line the predator left embedded in Solari culture so it could consume their devotion alongside their spirit's embers. They advocate extinguishing the Sol's Breath entirely and beginning a new covenant.

The Scoured, named for the forge-marks they ritually deface from their skin upon joining, have left both bloodlines entirely. They are scattered across Sundale, gathering fragments of the binding seal (the Sundered Monoliths) in the belief that if Keth Amar's breach can be sealed, Sol may finally be released from its endless suffering. They are regarded as dangerous fanatics by the tending-clan, as noble fools by the Sunderer, and as a quiet hope by the Anhur who fear the Sol's Breath's extinction.

The Anhur, who spend more time on the surface than any Korr, were the first to notice the evidence: ashfall shifting, vents cooling, the temperature dropping year by year. They are agitating for transparency. The Korr are refusing. The surface outposts and frontier settlements are caught between the two bloodlines, unsure which way the crisis will break.

Thaeron, the eldest Sun-Speaker, belongs to none of these camps. He has spent sixty years staring into the Sol's Breath's light, and he has seen something in it that does not match any faction's theology. He has told no one what he believes. He is waiting, as Solari have always waited, for Sol to speak again and settle the matter. But Sol has been silent for centuries, and Thaeron is old, and the ember is dimming faster than anyone alive can explain.
solari.culturalPractices:
The Marking-Rite is the foundation of Solari identity. At birth, every Solari's forearms and shoulders are marked by the clan's eldest Sun-Speaker using a heated obsidian stylus, deliberate burn-scars that encode three things: clan affiliation, trade specialization, and ancestor-lineage. The process is painful and brief. The child is not comforted during the marking; to cry out is normal, but to be soothed through the pain is considered a failure of the clan to prepare its young for the world. The marks darken with proximity to the Sol's Breath, Korr forge-marks are stark and crisp, while Anhur marks are fainter. This is not a flaw. It is a visible record of where the bloodline has stood in relation to Sol's ember across generations. To deface a forge-mark, cutting, burning over, or magically removing the scars, is the severest crime in Solari legal code, considered equivalent to erasing the victim from living memory.

The Vault-Breath is the discipline of absolute stillness and devotional contemplation. Children learn it before they learn speech: sitting motionless for increasing periods in the forge-halls, breathing in slow, deliberate cycles that conserve oxygen and quiet the mind before the Sol's Breath. An adult Solari can remain perfectly still for six hours, the length of a standard Sol's Breath tending-shift. Outsiders find this deeply unsettling. Among Solari, fidgeting is considered a sign of poor discipline, poor upbringing, or both. A guest who cannot sit still during a formal meeting has insulted the host, whether they know it or not.

The Eye-Wrap is a practical adaptation with deep cultural weight. Solari eyes, enlarged during the underground exile to see in near-total darkness, are painfully sensitive to daylight. Every adult wears a strip of ash-tinted cloth wrapped across the eyes, dyed with volcanic particulate that filters sunlight to tolerable levels. The wrap is personalized: clan colors, trade-sigils, and achievement-marks are woven into the fabric. Removing a Solari's eye-wrap without permission is a violation akin to stripping someone naked in public. Seeing a Solari without their wrap is an intimacy reserved for family, bonded partners, and deathbed confessions.

The Solstice Vigil occurs once each year during the longest period of darkness. Every forge-clan extinguishes all flames except the Sol's Breath. The entire clan, from the eldest Sun-Speaker to the youngest child, sits in the Vault-Breath for twelve hours of uninterrupted silence, listening for Sol's voice in the ember. No one has heard anything for centuries. The Vigil continues because stopping it would mean admitting Sol is truly gone. At the Vigil's end, newborns receive their forge-marks from the heated stylus, and the clan's forges are relit from the Sol's Breath's flame, a ritual that binds every Solari forge to the same source, the same vigil, the same silence.

Forge-trials settle disputes between clans. No Solari may strike another Solari in anger, this is the first clause of the Forge Accords, and violation means permanent exile. Disputes are instead resolved through competitions of craft, endurance, or stillness: who can forge the finest blade from raw obsidian, who can hold the Vault-Breath longest, who can recite the longest ancestor-lineage from memory without error. The nature of the trial is agreed upon by both parties. The loser accepts the verdict without appeal, because to dispute a forge-trial is to dispute the forge itself, and the forge is Sol's altar.

sharedTraits.name: Cold Vulnerability
sharedTraits.description: Vulnerable to cold/rime damage. Take +50% rime damage and have disadvantage on saves against environmental cold.

effects.name: Cold Vulnerability
effects.description: Vulnerable to rime damage. Take +50% rime damage.
effects.mechanicsText: Grants vulnerability to rime damage, causing you to take +50% increased damage from all rime sources. Also imposes disadvantage on saving throws against environmental cold.

sharedTraits.name: The Vault-Breath
sharedTraits.description: Your stillness is a weapon and a vulnerability, the discipline of centuries spent in oxygen-starved chambers, where every unnecessary motion burned air the vault could not spare. You can hold yourself motionless for hours, conserving air and quieting the mind, indistinguishable from the volcanic stone around you, and the mental discipline this requires grants you advantage on saves against fear and charm. But the deep stillness cannot be shed quickly. When combat begins, you make initiative rolls with disadvantage. Your body needs a moment to remember that movement is permitted.

effects.name: Forged Stillness
effects.description: Advantage on saving throws against fear and charm effects.

statusEffect.description: Advantage on fear and charm saves

effects.mechanicsText: Grants advantage on all saving throws against fear and charm effects, reflecting the mental discipline of the Vault-Breath.

effects.name: Deep-Vault Slowness
effects.description: Disadvantage on initiative rolls. Your body needs a moment to warm up and move.
effects.mechanicsText: Imposes disadvantage on initiative rolls when combat begins, as your body needs a moment to transition from deep stillness to movement.

sharedTraits.name: Ash-Lung
sharedTraits.description: Your lungs are lined with thick mucosal membranes, developed across generations of underground exile to filter toxic ash and particulate. You are immune to the effects of volcanic ashstorms, dust-clogging, and gas-based environmental hazards that would suffocate other races. But in clean, humid environments, your lungs grow heavy and sluggish, they lack the dry soot they adapted to filter.

effects.name: Ash-Filter
effects.description: Immune to the effects of volcanic ash, dust-choking, and gas-based environmental hazards.

statusEffect.description: Immune to airborne choking hazards

effects.mechanicsText: Grants full immunity to volcanic ash, dust-choking, and gas-based environmental hazards that would otherwise suffocate or obstruct breathing.

effects.name: Humidity Fatigue
effects.description: Disadvantage on endurance and constitution checks in humid or rainforest climates. Your lungs grow heavy in clean, damp air.
effects.mechanicsText: Imposes disadvantage on endurance and constitution checks while in humid or rainforest climates, as the ash-filtering lungs grow heavy in clean, damp air.

korr.name: Korr
korr.illustrationCaption: “In absolute stillness, the ember whispers what words cannot hold. We breathe with the fire; we do not command it.” — Cinder-Monk Meditation Maxim

illustrations.caption: “In absolute stillness, the ember whispers what words cannot hold. We breathe with the fire; we do not command it.” — Cinder-Monk Meditation Maxim
“Chiseled from living stalactites before the second age, the Grotto stands where the first ember was caught and held in reverence.” — Lore of the First Hearth
“A pilgrim does not measure the road by miles, but by how many hearths were rekindled along the way.” — High Prior Thaeron
“Let the basalt strike true; our faith is not a whisper, but an iron pact grounded in the rock.” — Templar-Warden Malthor
“Between the volcanic steam and the cool stone, the Sol’s Breath awakens the spirit to ancient memory.” — Vault Liturgy

korr.visualDescription: The fewest and the most deep-adapted. Korr skin is dark brown-beige, untouched by daylight, marked with the most elaborate ash-branding patterns of any Solari bloodline, stark and crisp from centuries of proximity to the Sol's Breath. Their enormous solid-black eyes are enlarged to read faint heat in absolute darkness, and their metabolisms are so slow their pulses are barely perceptible. Their bodies are conditioned for absolute stillness: elongated air-conserving lungs, dense bone, and a bearing so motionless that a sitting Korr can be mistaken for a carved votive. They wear their dreadlocks long and their ash-cloths thick against a daylight that pains them.
korr.tooltipSummary: Deep-vault forge-priests and Sun-Speakers, contemplative and deliberate, conditioned to absolute stillness before the Sol's Breath.
korr.description: The fewest and the most isolated. Korr bodies are conditioned for absolute stillness, elongated lungs that conserve air, metabolisms so slow their pulses are barely perceptible, and solid black eyes enlarged to perceive the faint heat in absolute darkness. Their skin is dark brown-beige, untouched by daylight, marked with the most elaborate ash-branding patterns, stark and crisp from proximity to the Sol's Breath. They are contemplative, scholarly in their devotion, spending their lives deciphering the Sol's Breath's silence. They move like people who have forgotten why movement matters. Their Vault-Breath can extend to twelve hours, double the standard, and older Korr report that time itself feels different in the deep, that centuries pass like seasons, and that the silence of the Sol's Breath is a language they are still learning to translate.
korr.culturalBackground:
The Korr trace their lineage to the Sun-Speakers who answered Sol's silence with absolute patience. When the other clans asked what they would contribute to the survival effort, the Korr answered: meaning. They would wait. For centuries, the other two clans fed them, protected them, and carried geothermal fuel down into the Deep-Vault where the air was too thin for anyone but a Korr to breathe, because the Korr were the Solari's connection to the dying heat. Without them, the survival effort had no purpose.

The Korr are the smallest bloodline and the most politically powerful. They hold the Sol's Breath. They interpret the silence. They officiate the Solstice Vigil and apply the newborn's forge-marks and determine, through decades of listening, whether a given omen means war or peace or nothing at all. Their word is final, because no other clan can perform the tending. The Vault-Breath required to endure the Deep-Vault for more than an hour is a Korr-specific adaptation; a Anhur who attempts the full vigil risks freezing.

The current crisis is a Korr crisis. The tending-clan has concealed the Sol's Breath's dimming for three generations, and the Sun-Speakers are no longer unified. Some still believe Sol will speak again. Some believe the ember is Keth Amar's tether and must be extinguished. Some, the Scoured, have defaced their marks and left the Deep-Vault entirely. Thaeron, the eldest Korr, has told no one what he believes. He is still listening.

traits.name: The Listening Dark
traits.description: Gain heat-sight: treat dim light as bright within 30 ft and total darkness as dim light within 60 ft, perceiving residual heat traces. However, you suffer disadvantage on all sight-based perception checks in bright light. The Sol's Breath's light reshaped your eyes across generations and left them unable to forgive the sun.

effects.name: Heat-Sight
effects.description: Treat dim light as bright within 30ft and total darkness as dim light within 60ft. Perceive residual heat traces.

statusEffect.description: Enhanced dark vision with heat perception

effects.mechanicsText: Enhances vision in darkness: dim light is treated as bright within 30 ft and total darkness as dim light within 60 ft, allowing perception of residual heat traces.

effects.name: Daylight Pain
effects.description: Disadvantage on all sight-based perception checks in bright light.
effects.mechanicsText: Imposes disadvantage on all sight-based perception checks while in bright light, as the dark-adapted eyes are pained by unfiltered daylight.

traits.name: The Sol's Breath's Pulse
traits.description: Advantage on spirit checks when within 1 mile of the Sol's Breath; -2 to concentration checks when the ember gutters (DM discretion). The pressure at the base of your skull is the Sol's Breath's pulse, and you cannot tell where you end and it begins.

effects.name: Ember Proximity
effects.description: Advantage on spirit checks when within 1 mile of the Sol's Breath

statusEffect.description: Advantage on spirit checks near the Sol's Breath

effects.mechanicsText: Grants advantage on spirit checks while within 1 mile of the Sol's Breath, attuned to its faint pulse.

effects.name: Shared Failing
effects.description: -2 to concentration checks when the Sol's Breath gutters during moments of crisis
effects.mechanicsText: Imposes a -2 penalty to concentration checks when the Sol's Breath gutters during moments of crisis, as its dimming frays your focus.

traits.name: Deep-Curse
traits.description: -5 ft movement speed, you cannot swim (you sink in water), and disadvantage on saving throws against cold effects. The oxygen-starved Deep-Vault that sheltered your ancestors kept you alive at the cost of leaving your marrow fragile to the very cold it was built to escape.

effects.name: Vault-Weight
effects.description: -5ft movement speed. Your bones are dense from the deep.
effects.mechanicsText: Reduces your movement speed by 5 ft, as your dense, deep-vault bones weigh you down.

effects.name: Cold-Seeped
effects.description: Disadvantage on saving throws against cold effects.

statusEffect.description: Disadvantage on cold saves

effects.mechanicsText: Imposes disadvantage on saving throws against cold effects, due to fragile marrow left vulnerable by the oxygen-starved Deep-Vault.

effects.name: Stone-Blood
effects.description: Cannot swim. You sink in water.

statusEffect.description: Swim speed is 0; you sink

effects.mechanicsText: You cannot swim and sink in water, as your stone-dense body has no buoyancy.

traits.name: Vault-Breath Exhale
traits.description: Once per short rest, exhale a concentrated burst of geothermal vapor in a 15-foot cone. All creatures in range must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 13) or be disoriented for 1 round. The Vault-Breath that sustains your stillness can also be weaponized.

effects.name: Disoriented
effects.description: Target must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 13) or be disoriented for 1 round. The geothermal vapor overwhelms the senses.

statusEffect.description: Disoriented for 1 round on failed Constitution save (DC 13).

effects.mechanicsText: Forces affected creatures to make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or be disoriented for 1 round, as the geothermal vapor overwhelms their senses.

thrask.name: Anhur
thrask.illustrationCaption: “The wind does not give warnings on the scree; only those who move like falling glass survive the ash.” — Sovereign Huntress Vaelith

illustrations.caption: “The wind does not give warnings on the scree; only those who move like falling glass survive the ash.” — Sovereign Huntress Vaelith
“The obsidian spearhead knows the scent of the dunes better than the eye can see.” — Scree-Runner Kaelen
“Where the pack lizards bed down and the smoke climbs into the night, the clan finds home upon the shifting ash.” — Anhur Camp Maxim
“Perched high above the sulfur vents, the Bastion watches the horizons for the shadows that hunt the badlands.” — Scree-Watch Annals
“Every drop wrung from the volcanic vapor is life bought back from the drought.” — Field Notes of the Ash-Scouts

thrask.visualDescription: The surface face of the Solari. Anhur bodies are leaner and more mobile than their deep-vault kin, built to range the volcanic ashlands rather than sit vigil in the dark. Their dark brown-beige skin is weathered from generations of surface exposure, and their ash-branding marks are fainter and blurred at the edges, softened by distance from the Sol's Breath. They shave their hair close and wrap themselves head to toe in heavy ash-insulating cloths against the cold of the open badlands, moving with the purposeful economy of scouts who have forgotten why stillness was ever necessary.
thrask.tooltipSummary: Surface scouts of the volcanic ashlands, leaner and more mobile than their deep-vault kin, carrying obsidian-forged tools across the scree.
thrask.description: The most surface-adapted and the most mobile. Anhur bodies have shorn hair and are wrapped in heavy ash-insulating cloths against the cold of the open ashlands. Their skin is dark brown-beige, weathered from surface exposure, and their ash-branding marks are fainter, blurred at the edges from generational distance from the Sol's Breath. Their ash-filtering lungs are somewhat weaker than the Korr's, adapted for the thin, cold air of the surface border rather than the thick particulate of the Mid-Vault. They are the Solari's connection to the surface, ranging the volcanic ashlands as scouts, messengers, and badland-hunters, mapping the thermal vents and carrying word between outposts. Leaner, faster, and more mobile than the Korr, they move like people who have forgotten why stillness was ever necessary.
thrask.culturalBackground:
The Anhur trace their lineage to the hunters who answered Sol's silence with vigilance. They worked the High-Vault, the tunnels nearest the frozen surface, ranging into the dead world above to hunt what survived the freeze and salvage active coal deposits. Without them, the other clans would have frozen in their sleep.

The Anhur are the Solari's connection to the surface, even now that the surface has been partially reclaimed. They map the ash-wastes, scout the frontier, and carry message-tubes between outposts. Vaelith, the most trusted messenger of the clans, is a Anhur.

The Anhur were the first to notice the evidence of the Sol's Breath's dimming. They spend more time on the surface, and they see the volcanic vents cooling and the glaciers encroaching. They are agitating for transparency and access to secondary heat resources. The Korr are refusing, fearing a panicked exodus that would deplete the Vault's core thermal grid.
thrask.currentCrisis: The surface thermal vents the Anhur depend on are cooling. Not everywhere or all at once, but the pattern is unmistakable: secondary geothermal fields that sustained Anhur outposts for centuries are dropping in temperature year by year. Anhur scouts have returned from the northern frontier reporting that entire vent-clusters have gone cold, their basalt crusts sealing over like healed wounds. The Anhur have begun migrating their outposts southward, closer to Emberspire's core heat, but that brings them into direct competition with Korr-claimed territories and the forge-clan hierarchy they have spent generations avoiding. The Korr refuse to acknowledge the cooling. The Anhur cannot ignore it. For the first time in centuries, the surface-scouts are being forced to choose: freeze on the frontier or submit to a Deep-Vault hierarchy that has never respected them.

traits.name: Border-Blood
traits.description: Advantage on saving throws against cold weather and environmental cold effects, but disadvantage on saving throws against heat effects and extreme heat. Your body learned to survive the border's cold by burning hotter, a threshold that cuts both ways and leaves you vulnerable to the fire your kin hoard.
