myrathil.name: Myrathil
myrathil.illustrationCaption: “In the depths where sunlight has never fallen, the nautilus lure guides the lost safely back to the trench.” — Sola the Glider
myrathil.cardFlavor: Sea-spawned from volcanic foam and storm-surge, their bioluminescent skin shifts with every tide and mood.
myrathil.visualDescription: Lean and fluid, standing 5'3" to 5'9", with bronze skin marked by shifting bioluminescent color along the vein-lines — teal in calm, storm-grey when the pressure drops, brighter when emotions run high. Their eyes are enormous and ocean-blue, too large for their faces, perpetually squinting against light they were not built for. Webbing connects their fingers, flushing with blood when their marine nature surfaces. Their hair is dark and salt-crusted. They wear kelp-weave body-wraps that tighten when wet, net-knot shawls laced with sea-glass beads, and waxed canvas storm-capes. Salt dries on their lashes when newly spawned from the sea-foam.
myrathil.description:
**[The Bioluminescent Foam-Born]**, *Lashed to the bowsprit of an ice-locked clipper, a slender Myrathil navigator with bioluminescent teal skin guides the ship through a shifting channel in the frozen sea.*

Mareth's native foam-spawned people lived before the Star-Fall. Storms, tides and local conditions bring anatomically complete young into communities where they grow and mature. The post-Strike rupture of Emberspire expanded spawning conditions and population, not first existence. Chosen families teach craft, navigation and care; calling a finder mother or a teacher ancestor does not imply biological wombs. Bioluminescent skin, swimming webbing and ecological differences accompany both air and water breathing. They can build relationships and histories without inheriting a noble bloodline.
myrathil.overview:
When the sun was dragged beneath the earth and the oceans began their long, slow death, Mareth did not bargain with the Keth Amar as the noble families did. She did not sacrifice her children at northern peaks or trade summer for frozen glaciers. She simply endured. And in her endurance, she grew curious. The Myrathil are the sea's attempt at personhood, her experiment in giving her waters a voice, a shape, a will that could walk upon the land her tides could only touch.

Viable native Myrathil spawnings existed before the Star-Fall. Mareth's foam-born people have their own ecology and history. Emberspire's post-Strike rupture later changed spawning conditions and produced a population boom, not their first existence.

The great population boom came in the decades after Emberspire stabilized, when the Iceheart Sea reached its perfect, churning equilibrium of freezing wave and volcanic current. Myrathil spawned by the hundreds along every coastline. Drift-villages appeared on horizons where no sail had ever been seen. Mareth's lonely experiment had become a people.

Myrathil emerge as anatomically complete young who grow and mature, not instant adults. They breathe air and water and require species-appropriate hydration and pressure care. Finders, teachers and chosen kin can be called mothers or ancestors without biological wombs. Rest requirements differ by heritage: Corali can rest on land, while deeper and river traditions have their own water-care needs.

The Myrathil are lunar creatures as much as aquatic ones. The moons of Mythrill pull the tides, and the tides pull the Myrathil. Every aspect of their biology (spawning cycles, navigation, emotional states, rest patterns) is tied to lunar phases. During the new moon, when tidal forces are strongest and the ocean is darkest, the most powerful spawning events occur and the Nereid-spawned Myrathil are born. The full moon brings the highest tides and the strongest social energy; Corali Myrathil are most active, the Tide-Sings are loudest, and trade conditions are best. The waxing and waning phases are used for navigation, the Myrathil read lunar position the way land-folk read compasses, feeling the pull in their veins even miles from the coast. All Myrathil feel the moon the way land-folk feel the sun. It is their clock, their compass, and their emotional anchor. A Myrathil deprived of moonlight grows restless and disoriented, not as severely as a land-dweller deprived of sun, but noticeably.

They are uncommon, elusive, and deeply misunderstood. In port cities of Sundale they are exotic celebrities. In the Frostwood Reach they are considered spirits of the mist-choked coast. The Skald of Nordhalla view them with the same suspicion they reserve for anything that does not freeze. The Athien of the Bryngloom Forest, ever the pragmatists, simply ask what the Myrathil want to trade. And the Myrathil, patient, amused, ancient in a way that has nothing to do with individual lifespan, tolerate the attention of younger races with the quiet grace of a people who have watched civilizations rise and fall on shorelines they once called home.

Somewhere in the Treakous Oceanic Rift, where the waters plunge deeper than any living thing has measured, one of the 7 Sundered Monoliths rests in absolute darkness. The Myrathil know where it is. Nereid Listeners have hummed toward it for generations and received answers they do not share. What the shard whispers in the abyss, and what Mareth intends to do about it, is a secret kept by a people who have never needed the land's wars or the land's shards, and who may discover, very soon, that the land's problems have followed them into the deep.
quickFacts: Mareth's native foam-spawned people existed before the Star-Fall. Young emerge anatomically complete and still grow and mature; family is chosen care, not noble biological descent.

Amphibious and bioluminescent, their vein-colors shift with mood and atmospheric pressure. They breathe both air and sea, navigate by lunar pull, and cannot truly rest without submersion. Divided into Corali diplomats, Nereid mystics who hum into the abyss, and Ondine explorers who follow rivers inland.

Play a Myrathil to be born of freedom itself, answerable to no spirits, bound to no land, claimed by nothing but the tide. But the spawning gales are shifting north, land-folk are damming your rivers and stealing your children, and the Sundered Monolith in the deepest trench has begun to hum a new frequency.
myrathil.culturalBackground:
Myrathil society is built around coasts, not bloodlines. Since every Myrathil spawns alone from the sea, family is chosen, communities form around stretches of shoreline, migratory camps, or floating raft-villages far from land. Their culture is oral and sung, history passed through harmonics that carry over water. They measure time in tides, not clocks, “meet me at mid-ebb” is precise; “meet me at noon” is foreign.

They live in the intertidal zone, the war between sea and land where the tide conquers half their world twice daily. Permanent structures make no sense here. Dwellings are driftwood frames hung with living curtain-kelp, storm-sail canvas that folds down into shelter when gales hit, and submerged rest-chambers grown from cultivated coral. Possessions float on tethered buoy-nets beside sleeping pools. A Myrathil camp can be abandoned in an hour and rebuilt the same day.

Clothing is layered: kelp-weave body-wraps as a base layer, a living fabric cultivated in submerged gardens, tightening when wet and breathing when dry. Over this, salvaged sailcloth robes, net-knot shawls laced with sea-glass beads, and waxed canvas storm-capes for rough weather. Jewelry is found and grown both: polished coral, sea-smoothed stone, living shell-grafts worn on the body. Every item tells a story.

Their tools and craft follow the same philosophy, nothing dead, nothing permanent. Kelp-rope that rehydrates and seals its own knots underwater. Whalebone and salvage-iron tools beaten from anchor-steel and hull-bolts. Domesticated sea-creatures fill niches machines fill for other races: anchor-crabs hold moorings, light-squid illuminate submerged chambers, kelp-eels tend garden-beds. The sea provides the material; their skill turns it into culture.

But Myrathil are uncommon, not rare. Port cities on the Iceheart Sea coast see them regularly, and they have established permanent and semi-permanent settlements along every major coastline and river system: Salt-Hinge at the mouth of the Silver River, the Drift-Home raft-village tethered over a submerged volcanic ridge, the First Shore where more Myrathil have spawned than anywhere else, Brinewell on the Frostwood Reach coastline, and Rillmeet at the confluence of three rivers far inland. Still, exoticism breeds rumor. In port cities they are exotic celebrities, poets write of their “liquid eyes,” collectors pay fortunes for their sea-glass (real or fake), and noble families keep Myrathil lovers they will never marry. Spawning beaches become tourist sites during gale-season; the wealthy stake out the coastline hoping to witness a birth, and sometimes they steal the child. Myrathil in human cities learn to perform, to be the charming sea-folk the stories describe, and some never learn to stop. Those who refuse to perform are written off as feral.

Among themselves, the Myrathil are warm and direct. They are gullible and too honest at times, naive in the way of a people who have no concept of inheritance, ownership, or bloodline. They CAN lie; they are simply bad at it, because their culture values directness and has no framework for sustained deception. Their vein-colors shift with emotion, making them easy to read, but a skilled Myrathil can suppress the tell with effort. They are not lie-detectors. They are emotionally transparent people raised in a culture that never taught them to hide. They settle disputes by submerging together: arguments had floating in a tide pool resolve differently than arguments had on dry land. Their highest value is freedom, the right to drift where currents take them, to belong nowhere fully, to answer to no one but Mareth and each other.
myrathil.variantDiversity: The Myrathil are shaped by the water that births them. The Shore Myrathil spawn where waves hammer shore — mediators, traders, the face the world sees. The Nereid Myrathil spawn in open ocean — mystics and sea-herders who find land-folk exhausting. The Brook Myrathil spawn where freshwater meets salt — explorers and scouts who follow rivers inland and return with stories no other Myrathil could tell.

integrationNotes.actionPointSystem: Myrathil abilities focus on water adaptation, weather-sensing, and mobility. They are amphibious skirmishers and support characters who thrive near coasts and waterways.
integrationNotes.backgroundSynergy: Myrathil excel in backgrounds emphasizing exploration, trade, and maritime life. Their uncommon nature and exotic reputation create compelling social dynamics.
integrationNotes.classCompatibility: The Minstrel is the Myrathil class, and every branch of the water owns a different register of it: the Merryn sing the open sea, the Corali the boundary, the Ondine the current inland, and the Nereid the pressure-silence of the deep. Beyond the Choir, the Nereid are native to the Animist (drowned town-memory), the Apex (trench hunting), and the Augur (pressure-sight); the Corali are native to the Augur (reading what the tide returns) and the Revenant (the tide-kept); the Ondine are native to the Animist (confluence-listening) and the Augur (the current-haruspex). Other classes are not native to the water.
integrationNotes.landMotivation: Myrathil venture inland when their spawning beaches are threatened, when the sea-silence drives them from familiar coastlines, when the Sundered Monolith in the Treakous Rift hums a new frequency, or when land-folk dam rivers and steal Brook Myrathil spawn-sites. They have no land-claims and seek none — but the sea's problems have followed them upstream, and ignoring the land is no longer an option.

myrathil.diasporaVariation: Myrathil diaspora follows the water. The Shore Myrathil hold the Iceheart coast; the Brook Myrathil have migrated up every major river system and established small enclaves in inland ports as far as the Sundrift Vale's edge and the Bryngloom's peat-waterways. A Bryngloom Brook Myrathil develops darker, bog-tinted bioluminescence and a tolerance for still water that coastal kin find unsettling. The Nereid Myrathil do not diaspora, they are trench-bound and surface only under the current crisis. Merrowport is the only true mixed Myrathil-Merryn city; elsewhere Myrathil are small river-enclaves, increasingly silent as the sea-silence spreads upstream.
myrathil.meaningfulTradeoffs: Myrathil are amphibious and weather-attuned, with rest requirements tied to their subrace and proximity to water. They are gullible and emotionally transparent; they can lie, but their culture never taught them how, and their vein-colors make them easy to read. Their exotic reputation creates social complications. The further they travel from the sea, the more disconnected they become from Mareth and the tides that made them.

baseTraits.reproduction: Foam-spawned young; grow and mature under chosen/community care

sharedTraits.description: Must submerge in water daily. 24 hours without submersion causes -2 to all attributes and halves speed.

myrathil.epicHistory:
Viable native spawnings and Myrathil communities preceded the Star-Fall. Their early histories belonged to Mareth's ecology, not a generative belief-Loom or Keth's invention. Emberspire's later rupture changed local conditions and caused a population boom.

Then the sun was torn from the sky.

The oceans began to freeze. Mareth felt her body turning solid at the extremities, glaciers reaching down from the poles, ice sheets thickening across her surface. She could not bargain with Keth Amar as the noble families did. She had no firstborn to offer, no words the abyssal entity would understand. She could only wait, and hope, and keep trying to make children who might survive what was coming.

When Emberspire erupted, Mareth received her answer. The collision of volcanic heat and ancient ice was not destruction, it was catalyst. The churning, freezing waves of the Iceheart Sea became a cradle. The foam that had always been her birthing medium grew thick with potential. The gales that spawned her children lasted longer, struck harder, reached further. In the decades after Emberspire stabilized, Myrathil spawned by the hundreds along every coastline. Mareth's lonely experiment had become a population.

The early Myrathil lived entirely at sea, drifting on raft-villages woven from living kelp and cultivated coral. They had no contact with land-folk for generations, and they were not missed. The first encounter came when a Corali child walked ashore near a Frostwood Reach fishing village and a terrified fisherman threw a net over her, thinking she was a caught spirit. She talked her way out of it. That fisherman became the first land-folk to speak with a Myrathil, and the stories he told spread through every port on the coast.

What followed, in the early centuries of the Freezing Era, was a period the land-folk called the Collection. Land-folk did not fear the Myrathil, they coveted them. Sailors claimed Myrathil tears turned to pearls. Nobles wanted Myrathil servants as status symbols. Scholars from Sundale's academies wanted to dissect one. The Myrathil retreated to isolated coasts and deep-ocean rafts, avoiding land-folk for another century while the fever died down. It never fully died. Even now, a Myrathil walking into a port town draws stares, offers, and the occasional attempted kidnapping.

The Myrathil have never had wars among themselves. They have no territory to fight over, the sea belongs to everyone and no one, and their population remains too scattered for organized conflict. What disputes arise are settled by submersion: the parties float together in deep water and talk until Mareth drains the anger out of them. It has always worked.

The most significant event in recent Myrathil history was the Inland Expedition, when a group of Ondine followed a great river system hundreds of miles inland and mapped territory no Myrathil had ever seen, mountains, deserts, and land-folk who had never heard of the sea. The expedition proved that Mareth's children could survive far from her embrace, though not without cost. It also proved that the land held things the sea had never imagined.

notableFigures.name: Saelith of the First Tide
notableFigures.title: The Voice That Crossed
notableFigures.backstory:
Saelith was the first Corali to walk into a human port and refuse to perform. When the poets wanted to write about her eyes, she asked them what they paid their last human subject. When a noble offered her rooms in his manor, she asked if the offer came with a collar. She was not angry, Myrathil are rarely angry, but she was direct in a way that land-folk found profoundly uncomfortable.

She established the first permanent Myrathil trading post at the mouth of the Silver River, a place called Salt-Hinge where land-folk and sea-folk could meet as equals. She wrote the Salt-Hinge Accords: a set of agreements that any Myrathil entering a trade deal could invoke, guaranteeing fair exchange and safe passage back to the sea. Most port cities still honor the Accords, though some only because violating them noticeably coincides with bad weather.

Saelith died old, nearly two hundred, floating in the tide pool where she was spawned. She refused to be buried on land. The tide took her body out, and three days later a gale spawned three new Myrathil on the same beach. No one who knew her believes that was a coincidence.

notableFigures.name: Ulvir the Listen-Long
notableFigures.title: The One Who Heard Too Much
notableFigures.backstory:
Ulvir was Nereid, spawned in open ocean during a moonless gale and not found by other Myrathil for nearly a month. He arrived on a floating village-raft already half-grown, speaking only in the low-frequency hum that Nereid use underwater. It took him a year to learn spoken language. His first words were: "The bottom is speaking."

What Ulvir heard in the abyss became the foundation of Nereid mysticism. He described voices, not spirits, not ancestors, but something older than both, something sleeping in the trenches where light has never reached. He taught other Nereid how to listen for these voices without losing themselves to them. Some of his students went too deep and never returned. Ulvir himself spent his last decades on a raft tethered over the deepest trench he could find, humming into the dark and listening for answers.

His teachings are controversial. Corali find them unsettling. Ondine dismiss them as deep-water delirium. But every Nereid Oracle traces their lineage of listening back to Ulvir, and every few generations another Myrathil comes up from a long dive with the same words: "It spoke again."

notableFigures.name: Venn the Salt-Walker
notableFigures.title: The One Who Found the Inland Sea
notableFigures.backstory:
Venn was Ondine, spawned in a brackish delta where three rivers met the sea. From childhood she was drawn inland, not toward the sea like most Myrathil, but upstream, following the taste of freshwater thinning into something else. At sixteen she left her delta camp and walked upriver alone. She was gone for three years.

She returned with maps, real maps, on parchment, bought from land-folk cartographers she'd befriended along the way. She had followed the Great River system to its headwaters in the Stonecrown Mountains, crossed a desert by following a seasonal stream that no map recorded, and discovered a vast inland lake that she named the Mother's Mirror, a body of water so large she couldn't see the far shore, and so deep she couldn't dive to its bottom. The lake had no salt. It was fresh. And when she submerged in it, she could rest.

Venn proved that Ondine could survive anywhere there was water, and her maps became the foundation for every Myrathil expedition inland. She died on her fifth expedition, somewhere in a mountain range she never finished naming, her body never found. Ondine still set out in her direction, hoping to complete her maps. None have.

majorLocations.name: The First Shore
majorLocations.description:
A crescent of white shell-grit beach on the western coast where more Myrathil have spawned than any other location. The sea here foams brighter during gales, visible from miles away, and the beach itself is littered with small cairns, each one marking where a Myrathil first stood up. No one builds permanent structures on the First Shore. It is a pilgrimage site, not a settlement. Myrathil visit to leave offerings (sea-glass, shells, a strand of their own kelp-weave) and to float in the tide pools where their kind first learned to exist.

Land-folk are not forbidden from the First Shore, but they rarely stay long. Something about the place makes them feel watched. The Myrathil say it is Mareth, curious about her guests.

majorLocations.name: The Drift-Home
majorLocations.description:
A sprawling raft-village tethered over a volcanic ridge, Drift-Home is the largest surface-adjacent Nereid community. The deep civic center is the Sunless Basalt Trench. Coral platforms, kelp bridges and cultivated marine life connect different depths rather than proving every Nereid lives on a surface raft.

The Drift-Home is the spiritual center of Nereid culture. The Listeners (those who practice Ulvir's teachings) maintain a submerged chamber at the village's center where they hum into the abyss and record what answers. Surface-folk who visit describe the experience as "floating on a cathedral made of living things."

majorLocations.name: Salt-Hinge
majorLocations.description:
The trading post Saelith founded at the mouth of the Silver River, now the largest permanent Myrathil settlement and the only place where land-folk and sea-folk conduct regular commerce as equals. Salt-Hinge is built on stilts over a tidal estuary, half submerged, half above water, with docks that lower and rise with the tide. Myrathil traders sell sea-glass jewelry, cultivated pearls, salted fish, and kelp-weave fabric. Land-folk traders sell forged tools, parchment, spices, and news.

Salt-Hinge operates under the Accords Saelith wrote, and both sides enforce them. The Myrathil who live here permanently are mostly Corali. It is the place where young Ondine come to buy supplies before walking inland, and where old Ondine return to sell their maps.

myrathil.currentCrisis:
The spawning gales are shifting. For centuries, the First Shore has been the most reliable birthing ground, producing more Myrathil than any other coastline. But over the last two generations, the gales have been moving north, further north each season, and the spawnings have followed them. The First Shore is not barren, but it is quieter than it has ever been. Mareth is moving her storms. Something is pulling them.

The Nereid Listeners who hum into the Treakous Oceanic Rift report that the Sundered Monolith resting at the bottom of that lightless chasm has changed its resonance. For generations it hummed at a frequency the Listeners could ignore, a background note in the deep. Now it thrums like a plucked string, and every Nereid within a hundred miles of the rift can feel it in their teeth. The Shard is awake. No one knows what woke it. Some Listeners whisper that the Keth Amar, slowly devouring the sun's embers in the world's core, has finally turned its attention to the pieces of the bargain it left scattered across the world. Others say Mareth herself is calling the Shard, that she has decided, after millennia of patience, that the time for watching has passed.

Meanwhile, the threats from the surface world multiply. Ondine who have traveled far inland report that land-folk are damming rivers, draining marshes, and building ports over spawning estuaries without knowing, or caring, what they are destroying. A noble house in the eastern kingdoms has begun offering bounties for live Myrathil, claiming scholarly purposes while their menagerie tells a different story. A new port city has been proposed directly on top of a minor spawning beach near the Frostwood Reach coastline. Land-folk tourism to gale-season sites has become an industry, the wealthy staking out the coast during storms, hoping to witness a birth, and sometimes stealing the child.

The Myrathil are not endangered, not yet. But for the first time in their history, they are asking whether Mareth can keep up with a world that has forgotten to fear the ocean.

The Corali want to negotiate, to establish treaties and accords with the land-kingdoms before the situation escalates. The Nereid want to disappear into the open ocean, to drift so far from shore that no land-folk ship could ever find them. The Ondine want to map every spawning site, every estuary, every brackish delta before it is destroyed, to preserve at least the knowledge of what was lost if the losses cannot be prevented.

All three answers may be right. None of them may be enough. And beneath the churning, freezing waves of the Iceheart Sea, the Sundered Monolith hums its new, urgent frequency into the dark, waiting for whatever comes to claim it.

The Myrathil have never needed the land's wars or the land's shards — but the land's wars have followed them into the deep. The same Monolith that hums in the Rift is kin to the shards the Dawn Vigil hunts and Keth Amar feeds through; if the seal fails, no ocean depth will protect what spawns in its waters. Mareth's children must choose: drift away while the world above burns, or rise and wade into a war that was never theirs.
myrathil.culturalPractices:
Every Myrathil child spawns alone and walks ashore with nothing but salt in their hair and the sea's last foam clinging to their heels. They are found, always found, by other Myrathil, because the signs of a spawning are unmistakable. Tide pools arrange shells in spirals. Shorebirds circle silently. The waves sound spoken. Any Myrathil within twenty miles feels the ache in their veins. The community gathers before the child even opens its eyes.

The first words a Myrathil hears are their own name, spoken by whoever reaches them first. Myrathil names are not inherited, they are given fresh each time, chosen by the finder, based on something about the child or the spawning conditions. A child spawned under a full moon might be named Luneth. One spawned in a gale that tore ships apart might be named Brekka.

The first submersion is the most important ritual in a Myrathil's life. Within hours of spawning, the child is carried into the sea and submerged completely, not to drown, but to wake up. Myrathil breathe water as easily as air, but submersion triggers something deeper: their nervous system calms, their vein-colors stabilize, and they truly sleep for the first time. The submersion is done by the finder, who holds the child underwater and hums. Every Myrathil remembers their first submersion as a feeling, not a memory, the moment the world stopped being loud.

Adolescence is marked by the First Drift: a young Myrathil leaves their community and follows the coast or the current for a full season, alone, carrying only what they can float behind them. Some go inland. Some go deep. Some never come back, but most do, returning with stories, scars, and the right to speak at community gatherings. The First Drift is what turns a Myrathil child into a Myrathil adult.

The Tide-Share is the core of Myrathil community life. Every evening at mid-flood, the community gathers, on the shore, on the raft-decks, on the riverbank, and shares what they found that day: fish, salvage, news, stories. Nothing is traded; everything is given. A Myrathil who hoards is sick, and the community responds by submerging them, literally carrying them into the water and holding them there until they remember they are not alone.

The Tide-Sing occurs at spawning gales. When a storm approaches that carries the right pressure and the right wind, Myrathil gather on the nearest coast and sing, not to summon the storm, but to welcome whatever it brings. During the Tide-Sing, Myrathil do not speak in words. They hum. The harmonics layer and build until every Myrathil present is breathing in the same rhythm at the same moment. Mareth, they believe, can hear them. Sometimes the gale spawns a child. Sometimes it doesn't. Either outcome is accepted with the same quiet grace.

birthrightQuestions.description: At character creation, choose one of the following RP prompts to define what was unusual about your spawning. No mechanical effects, purely who you are and what you carry.

prompts.name: Witnessed
prompts.question: Someone was there when you stood up from the foam. A fisherman who helped you walk your first steps on sand. A terrified sailor who fled. Another Myrathil who stayed to name you. Whoever it was, their face was the first thing you saw. What is the nature of your bond to the one who saw you born?

prompts.name: The Second Storm
prompts.question: Your spawning gale lasted the usual three days, but at the exact moment you opened your eyes, a second storm-front hit from the opposite direction. The collision spiked the waves into chaos, and during that chaos, something spoke. You do not remember what it said. But sometimes, in the moment just before you fall asleep, you almost do. What do you think the voice was?

prompts.name: The Silence
prompts.question: Most Myrathil are born into howling wind and crashing surf. You were born into total calm. Your gale died the second your foam took shape. The sea went glassy-flat, the wind dropped to nothing, and you stood up in a world that had gone completely silent. Other Myrathil find this deeply unsettling. What do you think the silence meant?

prompts.name: The Drift
prompts.question: You did not spawn on a shore. You formed from foam in the open water and drifted for days before you found land. You have no birth-coast. No spawning-beach to return to. Just open ocean all around and a vague sense that you are still drifting. How do you answer when asked where you are from?

prompts.name: Twice-Born
prompts.question: Your foam took shape, you stood up, and then you collapsed back into the sea. Hours later, it happened again. Same storm, same shore, same foam. You stood up a second time, and this time you stayed. Other Myrathil consider this an omen, but cannot agree of what. Some say Mareth reconsidered and chose you twice. Some say you were not finished the first time. Which do you believe?

shoreling.name: Corali
shoreling.illustrationCaption: “Carved directly into the limestone cliffs of Salt-Hinge, our harbor stands firm against the highest storm surge of the solstice.” — Wave-Master Saelith

illustrations.caption: Salt-Hinge Harbor Fortress & Tidal Bazaar — Sovereign coastal trade metropolis carved into white limestone cliffs with aqueducts, boom-cranes, and conch lighthouses.
The First Shore & Spawning Cairns — Sacred ancestral emergence beach of crushed shell-grit with natural limestone tide-pools and weathered offering cairns.
The Spindrift Tide-Council Rotunda — Monumental open-air limestone pavilion perched on a wave-battered granite sea-stack where diplomats negotiate trade.
Corali Racial Portrait Bust — Noble coastal wave-guardian with windswept platinum wave-foam hair, scalloped wave-fin ears, neck gill-slits, and verdigris sea-bronze gorget.
Saelith of the First Tide — Legendary diplomat and founder of Salt-Hinge proclaiming the maritime Accords with bronze treaty tablet and driftwood wave-staff.
Commander Morvath of the Wave-Guard — Veteran breakwater defender bracing against a crashing breaker, pinning a thrashing leviathan tentacle with his driftwood wave-staff.
Envoy Talia Spindrift-Tongue — Chief maritime arbitrator pointing an accusing brass stylus onto a falsified nautical chart as her bioluminescent tidal veins flare.
Old Barnaby the Reef-Runner — Veteran barnacle-grip sentry caught in an explosive airborne leap across a foaming reef chasm, loosing a harpoon spear.
High Tide-Weaver Klynn — Grand animist channeling a spawning gale at the water’s edge, levitating a swirling vortex of sea-foam and cowrie shells around her driftwood wave-staff.

shoreling.visualDescription: Standing tall and athletic with a swimmer's reach, the Corali are built for the intertidal collision of land and sea. Their sun-kissed salt-bronzed skin carries faint iridescent nacre across the shoulders and shifting bioluminescent tidal veins along the clavicle and arms—serene teal in calm, storm-grey when barometric pressure plummets. Scalloped wave-fin ears fan back against ocean spray, and subtle neck gill-slits pulse with tidal rhythm beneath their jaw. Their piercing ocean-blue eyes squint against harsh sunlight, dried sea-salt crystals clinging to their lashes and silver-white braids. Five-fingered hands feature flexible swimming webbing, while their high-arched bare feet are webbed and textured to grip slick granite breakwaters and wave-battered reefs. They favor tailored wave-silk wraps, layered sailcloth, and practical storm-capes.
shoreling.tooltipSummary: Corali-born diplomats who broker deals between sea and land, their vein-colors betraying every emotion they cannot hide.
shoreling.description: The first Myrathil, spawned from the meeting of volcanic foam and glacial melt, ages before the sun was buried. The most numerous and the ambassadors their people present to the world. Born where waves hammer shore, the collision of sea meeting land, of volcanic warmth meeting glacial melt, of the Iceheart Sea's patient fury meeting the continents it can never quite claim. The Corali are the most numerous Myrathil, the ambassadors, the face their people present to a world that collects them. Their bodies are built for both worlds and belong fully to neither, lungs for air, gill-veins for water, webbed fingers that flush with blood when they remember what they are. Unlike their Nereid and Ondine kin, the Corali can long rest on dry land without submersion, though they recover faster and more fully when sleeping in salt water. They are the most adaptable Myrathil, the diplomats and traders who run trade posts and negotiate with port authorities. They broker deals between ship-captains and shore-towns in ports from Frostwood Reach to Sundale. They mediate disputes in tide pools and trading posts. They carry the weight of being the diplomats of a people who have no nations, no armies, and no exploit except the quiet threat that the sea, should she choose, could take back every coastline she ever lent to the land. The flaw they carry is the flaw of the middle: they mediate everyone else's conflicts but cannot resolve their own. A Corali who picks a side, land or sea, is seen as having failed at being Myrathil.
shoreling.culturalBackground: Corali are the most visible Myrathil in the wider world. They maintain the trade posts from Salt-Hinge to the Frostwood Reach coast, negotiate with port authorities in cities that barely acknowledge their right to exist, and have developed a social fluency that other Myrathil find exhausting. They learn land-languages young, the tongues of Sundale, the trade-pidgins of the Iceheart Sea routes, the formal speech of Athien merchants who have learned that a Myrathil trader is more reliable than a human one. Their camps are the most permanent, relatively speaking, and their kelp-weave tends toward the practical and presentable rather than the ceremonial. They are the Myrathil most likely to marry into land-settlements, most likely to have human friends, and most likely to wake up at night in a dry bed feeling the tide pull in two directions at once. When the Sundered Monolith in the Treakous Rift began its new resonance, it was Corali who carried the news to every Myrathil community along every coastline within a month. It is Corali who now carry the difficult questions: negotiate or retreat? Treaty or disappearance? Mareth is not answering. She has never answered directly. She only sends more storms.

traits.name: Born of Spindrift
traits.description: You gain Water Breathing and a +30 ft swim speed. Long resting in salt water for 4+ hours provides full HP recovery; long resting on land without submersion yields only half normal HP recovery. Mareth gave you lungs for air and gill-veins for water, but only the tide's weight lets you truly sleep.

effects.description: Breathe both air and water without limitation.
effects.mechanicsText: Grants the Water Breathing trait, permitting unhindered breathing in both air and water at all times.

effects.name: Natural Swimmer
effects.description: +30ft swim speed. The sea recognizes her children.
effects.mechanicsText: Adds a flat +30 ft to the creatures swim speed, making movement through water swift and natural.

effects.name: Surface Restlessness
effects.description: Long resting without at least 4 hours of salt-water submersion provides only half the normal HP recovery; full submersion provides full recovery.
effects.mechanicsText: Without at least 4 hours of salt-water submersion in a day, long resting restores only half normal HP; with submersion, full HP is restored.

statusEffect.description: Long resting without salt-water submersion provides half HP recovery. Full submersion for 4+ hours restores full HP.

traits.name: Storm-Blooded
traits.description: During storm conditions (rain, gale, thunder, heavy sea) you gain +2 Initiative. You always know the direction of the nearest major body of water and can sense incoming storms up to 72 hours ahead — their direction, intensity, and arrival time. Your vein-colors surge and your blood wakes at the sky's first pressure-change; the spawning weather that made you left a permanent sensitivity to the storm.

effects.name: Storm Surge
effects.description: +2 Initiative during storm conditions (rain, gale, thunder, heavy sea). The storm is your element.
effects.mechanicsText: During storm conditions, this grants a flat +2 bonus to Initiative, reflecting the creature’s attunement to wild weather.

selectedEffects.name: Weather Sense
selectedEffects.description: Always know the direction of the nearest major body of water. Can sense incoming storms up to 72 hours in advance, their direction, approximate intensity, and when they will arrive.

traits.name: Tide-Tongue
traits.description: You gain +1 to Insight and Persuasion checks. Your vein-colors shift with strong emotion, making you easy to read, but you CAN suppress the tell with effort and you CAN lie; your culture simply never taught you how. You feel the emotional currents in a room like weather patterns, and you learned early that the truth, delivered gently, is a currency most have forgotten how to spend.

effects.name: Emotional Currents
effects.description: +1 to Insight and Persuasion checks. You read people like weather patterns.
effects.mechanicsText: Grants a +1 bonus to Insight and Persuasion checks, letting the creature read emotional currents like weather patterns.

statusEffect.description: +1 Insight, +1 Persuasion

traits.name: Spindrift Diplomacy
traits.description: Advantage on Persuasion checks during trade negotiations or diplomatic mediations; failing to mediate a conflict between two parties who share your loyalty deals you 1 wyrd damage. Corali carry the middle between sea and land, reading a room the way you read a tide chart — but the middle is a lonely place, and Mareth does not judge those who try to hold it.

effects.name: Trade Mediator
effects.description: Advantage on Persuasion during trade or mediation.
effects.mechanicsText: Grants advantage on Persuasion checks made during trade negotiations or diplomatic mediations.

effects.name: The Bridge That Could Not Hold
effects.description: 1 wyrd damage when you fail to mediate a conflict between parties who share your loyalty.
effects.mechanicsText: When mediation of a conflict between two loyal parties fails, the creature takes 1 point of wyrd damage.

statusEffect.description: 1 wyrd damage on failed mediation.

deepling.name: Nereid
deepling.illustrationCaption: “In the crushing silence of the abyss, the trench spires sing with the pressure of a thousand fathoms.” — Deep-Council Chronicler

illustrations.caption: The Sunless Basalt Trench Metropolis — Sunken underwater chasm metropolis built between sheer vertical basalt cliffs with hexagonal spires and hydrothermal bubble chimneys.
The Ulvir Acoustic Resonance Chambers — Monumental vaulted nave carved out of abyssal basalt where acoustic organ flutes funnel pressure currents.
The Drift-Home — Open-ocean floating coral raft-cathedral tethered over submerged volcanic seamounts to colossal anchor-crabs.
Sola the Glider — Youthful Nereid Myrathil ambassador holding a nautilus-shell light-lure beacon with swirling companion baby squids.

deepling.visualDescription: Abyss-adapted organic people with buoyant, current-balanced movement, not literal zero gravity. Pearlescent-indigo skin carries cyan photophores and visible capillary patterns; dark indigo eyes with luminous pupils read the lightless deep. Translucent mantle-fin ears, neck gill-slits, forearm finlets and pressure-cured kelp-silk preserve the deep-water silhouette. Young require growth, care and appropriate pressure adaptation, not instant adulthood.
deepling.tooltipSummary: Abyss-born mystics who hum into the ocean trench and speak a language older than words, finding the surface world unbearably loud.
deepling.description: Emerged in the first century of the Freezing Era as the Iceheart Sea reached thermal equilibrium. Abyss-adapted mystics who hum into the Treakous Rift. Born from foam in the open Iceheart Sea during moonless gales, far from any coast. Sometimes they drift for weeks before finding land, arriving on beaches already half-grown, salt-crusted, speaking only the low-frequency hum that Myrathil use underwater. Their biology skews further toward sea than their Corali kin: longer submersion tolerance, stronger swimming muscles, less comfort with spoken language. They must hydrate frequently; prolonged dryness is exhausting, and after 24 hours in arid conditions cumulative fatigue sets in. Moist or humid environments suffice for comfort, but they need proximity to water for a true long rest. Being dry is not dangerous, but it is draining, like holding your breath: they can do it, but they would rather not. They are the mystics who hum into the Treakous Rift and record what answers, the sea-herders who tend the deep kelp-forests and migration routes, the guardians of knowledge the surface world would call madness and they call home. The flaw they carry is distance: land-folk feel alien and exhausting to them, their customs incomprehensible, their desperate need to fill silence with speech a constant irritation. A Nereid who spends too long on land begins to feel their own heartbeat as an intrusion, a reminder that they carry something warm inside them, and warmth is not what the deep prepared them for.
deepling.culturalBackground: Nereid communities are the most isolated of all Myrathil. Their raft-villages drift far from shipping lanes, tethered over submerged volcanic ridges where the water runs warmer and the kelp grows thicker. Their submerged rest-chambers are too deep for surface-folk to reach without magic. Their culture is built around listening rather than speaking, the Ulvir tradition of humming into the abyss and recording what answers. When the Sundered Monolith in the Treakous Rift changed its resonance, the Nereid were the first to know. They had been listening to it for generations: a background hum, constant and ignorable. Now it thrums with purpose, and every Nereid within a hundred miles can feel it. The elders debate what this means. Some say the Shard is calling to its siblings, that the 7 Shards are waking, one by one, and the Myrathil have been guardian of one for millennia without knowing it. Others say the Shard is calling to Mareth herself, and that she is finally preparing to answer. Many Nereid go their entire lives without speaking to a non-Myrathil. They prefer the low hum. The surface world is unbearably loud.

traits.name: Born of Spindrift
traits.description: You gain Water Breathing and a +30 ft swim speed. True rest requires 4+ hours of submersion in salt water; sleeping on land yields only half normal HP recovery. Mareth gave you lungs for air and gill-veins for water, but you are not equally at home on land — only the weight of the deep lets you truly sleep.

effects.description: Breathe both air and water without limitation.
effects.mechanicsText: Grants the Water Breathing trait, permitting unhindered breathing in both air and water at all times.

effects.name: Natural Swimmer
effects.description: +30ft swim speed. The sea recognizes her children.

effects.mechanicsText: Without at least 4 hours of salt-water submersion in a day, the creature cannot benefit from a long rest; sleeping on land restores only half normal HP.

traits.name: Abyssal Adaptation
traits.description: While submerged you gain Darkvision 60 ft, 25% Cold Resistance, and can hold your breath for 30 minutes. Every 12 hours continuously on land without submersion costs -1 to all ability checks (cumulative, max -3), resetting the moment you submerge in salt water. The deep left its mark on your body — lungs that compress without pain, eyes built for absolute dark, skin that barely feels the cold that kills surface-swimmers.

effects.name: Deep Sight
effects.description: Darkvision 60ft while submerged. The abyss has no light, so Mareth gave you different eyes.
effects.mechanicsText: While submerged, the creature gains Darkvision out to 60 ft, seeing in total darkness underwater.

statusEffect.description: Darkvision 60ft underwater

effects.name: Deep Cold
effects.description: 25% cold resistance while submerged. Deep water does not freeze, and neither do you.
effects.mechanicsText: While submerged, the creature gains 25% resistance to cold damage.

effects.name: Long Breath
effects.description: Can hold breath for 30 minutes. Your lungs were shaped by pressure.
effects.mechanicsText: The creature can hold its breath for 30 minutes before needing to breathe.

statusEffect.description: Hold breath 30 minutes

effects.name: Land-Sickness
effects.description: Every 12 hours spent continuously on land without submersion: -1 to all ability checks (cumulative, max -3). Resets immediately upon submersion in salt water. The deep does not release its children without taking something back.
effects.mechanicsText: For every 12 consecutive hours on land without submersion, the creature suffers a cumulative -1 penalty to all ability checks, up to a maximum of -3, resetting the moment it submerges in salt water.

statusEffect.description: Accumulating -1 to all checks per 12hrs on land, max -3. Resets on submersion.

traits.name: The Nereid Hum
traits.description: Every Myrathil carries a secondary voice, a low-frequency hum that carries for miles underwater and just barely registers above the surface. Nereid learn to shape it. You can speak through it, sending simple concepts through the water to anyone in range. Above water, you can let it resonate through the air, a single low note that steadies the minds of those nearby. The hum is not language. It is older than language. It is what Mareth sounds like when she is listening.

effects.name: Resonant Hum
effects.description: While humming actively (costs 1 AP to start, free to maintain), allies within 30ft gain +1 to Spirit and Intelligence saving throws. The hum is audible, stealth is impossible while active.
effects.mechanicsText: While actively humming, allies within 30 ft gain a +1 bonus to Spirit and Intelligence saving throws; the audible hum prevents stealth.

statusEffect.description: +1 to SPR/INT saves for allies within 30ft while humming

selectedEffects.name: Sea-Call
selectedEffects.description: While submerged, can communicate simple concepts (danger, safety, direction, numbers, emotion) silently to any creature within 120ft underwater.

traits.name: Mareth's Hum
traits.description: Once per long rest you may enter a 1-minute uninterrupted humming trance to sense the emotional state and approximate location of all creatures within 100 ft touching the same body of water. On land, you must succeed a DC 10 Spirit save to benefit from a long rest without at least 1 hour of salt-water submersion. You carry Mareth's frequency in your bones, a low vibration aligning you with the deep currents and the creatures who navigate them.

effects.name: The Hum
effects.description: Once per long rest, sense creatures within 100ft in the same body of water via 1-minute trance.

selectedEffects.name: Water Sense
selectedEffects.description: Sense emotional state + approximate location of creatures within 100ft touching the same body of water. 1-minute trance.

effects.name: Surface Restlessness

effects.mechanicsText: Without at least 1 hour of salt-water submersion, the creature must succeed on a DC 10 Spirit save or gain no benefit from a long rest.

statusEffect.description: Spirit save DC 10 to benefit from long rest without salt water.

riverling.name: Ondine
riverling.illustrationCaption: “Suspended above the roaring gorge of Cataract Reach, the cypress timbers bend with the current but never break.” — River-Warden Venn

illustrations.caption: Cataract Reach — Sovereign multi-tiered cypress stilt-city spanning a roaring waterfall gorge with suspension bridges, waterwheels, and Ondine scout balconies.
Mother's Mirror — Vast, glassy-clear freshwater inland sea sanctuary framed by pine-covered mountain peaks, thatched pavilions, and dugout canoes.
Venn's Sluice-Way & Delta Market — Bustling wetland trading post built over river delta mudflats with raised boardwalks, timber sluices, and cargo barges.
Venn the Salt-Walker — Legendary pioneer explorer charting the inland sea with an unrolled waterway map, brass river-sextant, and dugout canoe.
Kaelen the Rapid-Leaper — Veteran trident scout balanced in a low amphibious perching crouch on rapid boulders with his barbed three-pronged gig trident.

riverling.visualDescription: The wanderers of the inland waters. Ondine are born of brackish spawning, river mouths, estuaries, mangrove deltas, and it shows in an athletic amphibious build tuned for freshwater travel: lean, agile, and sure-footed on wet riverbed boulders. Symmetrical, expressive facial features with strikingly large, luminous jade-green river-eyes are framed by smooth, moist frog-like river skin stippled with circular pebble-spots across the brow, temples, and cheekbones. Behind the temples and ears rise distinctive upward-branching antler-like fleshy river-tendrils with three to four smooth pronged branches resembling staghorn coral. Their broad amphibious hands and bare feet feature prominent translucent swimming webbing between long fingers tipped with rounded spatulate salamander adhesive suction pads that adhere securely to slick, mossy boulders, wet logs, and roaring rapids (strictly no claws). Their vein-colors run bright jade, fed by moving water, and they alone can submerge in freshwater without irritation. They favor light traveling clothes, pocketed leather scout vests, braided rope plaits with four-leaf water-clover pins, and parchment maps of waterways no one else charts.
riverling.tooltipSummary: Estuary-born explorers who follow rivers inland to map territories no Myrathil has ever seen, caught between two worlds that claim them.
riverling.description: Emerged in the early centuries of the Freezing Era when Venn the Salt-Walker discovered the Mother's Mirror and proved Myrathil could survive in freshwater. The wanderers who follow rivers inland. Born where freshwater meets salt, river mouths, estuaries, mangrove deltas, in brackish water that is neither one world nor the other. Unlike other Myrathil, they can submerge in freshwater without the salt-irritation that makes their kin avoid the rivers that vein the continents. This makes them the wanderers: the ones who follow waterways inland from the Frostwood Reach to the edge of Sundale's volcanic deserts, who have crossed the Sundrift Vale by following a seasonal stream that no map recorded, who become scouts and explorers seeing mountains for the first time in Myrathil history. They are the most adaptable and self-sufficient of the Myrathil, needing only some contact with water to sustain themselves where their kin require submersion. Their yearning is for flowing freshwater: a Ondine Myrathil who returns to a river after long absence feels the current in their veins reawaken, like a pulse finding its rhythm again. They return with maps and stories and a look in their eyes that other Myrathil find hard to hold. The flaw they carry is suspicion from their own kind. A Ondine who stays inland too long "forgets the taste of mother." Corali treat them as too land-ish. Nereid treat them as practically human. They are the ones caught between loyalties, accused of not being Myrathil enough, and yet they are the only Myrathil who have seen the inland territories where the Sundered Monoliths rest, who have walked the Sundrift Vale and mapped the rivers that flow toward the Bryngloom Forest's swampy heart.
riverling.culturalBackground: Ondine are the explorers of Myrathil society, but they are also the bearers of the most urgent intelligence. When word of the Sundered Monolith's awakening in the Treakous Rift reached the delta camps, it was Ondine who connected it to what they had seen inland: other old magics stirring, ancient burial mounds humming in the Sundrift Vale, a murky pool in the Bryngloom Forest that had begun to glow with light that did not behave like light. They follow rivers inland, trading with land-settlements far from the coast, mapping territories no other Myrathil has seen. Their camps are temporary, their possessions are minimal, and their relationships with land-folk are the most genuine, they are the Myrathil most likely to have human friends rather than human collectors. They return to the delta or coast every few years to share their maps and stories at the Tide-Share. Some settle inland permanently, marrying into land-communities and raising children who have never seen the sea. These are mourned as lost by their kin, even while they are still alive and happy, Mareth's children who chose the land, and whom the land, in its own way, accepted. When the crisis over the spawning gales escalates, it will be the Ondine who carry the messages between the retreating Nereid and the negotiating Corali, as they have always carried the messages between worlds that do not speak the same language.
riverling.currentCrisis: The rivers are changing faster than any Ondine can map. The Great Silver River has dropped three feet in the last decade. Seasonal streams that have flowed since before the sun was buried are drying to gravel beds. Ondine who followed those streams inland, who built trading posts and lives far from the coast, are being forced to retreat — or to stay and watch the water vanish around them. The land-folk blame the volcanic winter shifting rainfall. The Nereid blame the Sundered Monolith in the Treakous Rift, its awakening pulling thermal currents in directions no one can predict. The Corali say nothing, because saying "we told you so" to a Ondine whose homeland is evaporating would be cruel. The Ondine are running out of rivers — and for the first time, asking whether Mareth ever intended them to go so far inland at all.

True rest otherwise requires 4+ hours of submersion; sleeping on land yields only half normal HP recovery. Your brackish spawning means the rivers welcome you where the sea cannot reach, and you breathe both air and water.

traits.name: Brackish Heritage

When more than 50 miles from any natural water source (river, lake, or coast), you lose 1 Spirit. Spawned where two waters meet, your body remembers the blend — but the further you travel from any water, the fainter Mareth's voice becomes in your chest.

effects.name: Brackish Blood
effects.description: Immune to negative effects from freshwater exposure that affect other Myrathil. Resistant to poison (25% damage reduction).
effects.mechanicsText: Grants immunity to freshwater-exposure effects that harm other Myrathil and 25% resistance to poison damage.

effects.name: River Swimmer
effects.description: +5ft movement speed when traveling along rivers or streams. You read currents the way others read roads.
effects.mechanicsText: While traveling along rivers or streams, the creature gains a flat +5 ft to its movement speed.

effects.name: Distant Waters
effects.description: When more than 50 miles from any natural water source (river, lake, or coast): -1 Spirit. Mareth's voice grows faint, and you feel it in your chest.
effects.mechanicsText: When more than 50 miles from any natural water source, the creature loses 1 point of Spirit.

statusEffect.description: -1 Spirit when >50 miles from natural water

traits.name: Mask of the Estuary
traits.description: The Ondine spend more time among land-folk than any other Myrathil, and they have learned to pull the sea inward when they need to pass unnoticed. You can retract your webbing completely, dim your vein-colors to near-invisibility, and still the restless tide in your movements until you look, briefly, almost human. It is uncomfortable, like holding your breath while awake, and you cannot maintain it forever. Mareth does not judge you for hiding. But she does not help, either.

traits.name: Fresh-Water Memory
traits.description: Advantage on Intelligence (History) or Survival checks to recall geographical features of any freshwater system you have personally traveled, and once per long rest you may perfectly retrace any river route you swam within the last week (even if blinded or disoriented); you suffer Disadvantage on Knowledge checks for land-based geography. Ondine carry maps no one else draws — every river lived in your blood as currents, not memories, a flowing cartography that surfaces when you need it most, though the land-folk's maps still make no sense to someone who navigates by flow.
